SUMMARY
This summary aims to give you an overview of the information contained in this prospectus. As
itisasummary,itdoesnotcontainalltheinformationthatmaybeimportanttoyou.Youshouldread
the whole prospectus before you decide to invest in the Offer Shares.
There are risks associated with any investment. Some of the particular risks in investing in the
OfferSharesaresetoutinthesectionheaded“RiskFactors”inthisprospectus.Youshouldreadthat
section carefully in full before you decide to invest in the Offer Share.
OVERVIEW
We are an electronic test and measurement instrument company in the PRC with advanced
technology capabilities and extensive global footprint. Electronic test and measurement instruments
are devices designed for observing, testing, measuring, and calculating a wide range of physical
parameters. These instruments are used to diagnose, test, and verify the performance of electronic
devices and components by analyzing key electrical characteristics such as electrical signals, voltage,
current, resistance, and frequency. We design, develop, manufacture and deliver a comprehensive
suite of electronic test and measurement instruments and solutions that power scientific discovery
and industrial innovation. According to Frost & Sullivan, we ranked eighth and are the largest PRC
electronic test and measurement instrument provider globally in terms of revenue in 2025, with a
marketshareof1.2%.WealsorankedsixthintheChinaelectronictestandmeasurementinstrument
market in terms of revenue in 2025, with a market share of 1.9%. Under the “RIGOL” brand, we
serve a diverse customer base of over 100,000 end customers across more than 90 countries and
regions, addressing complex test challenges across communications, new energy, semiconductors,
and education and research sectors.
Through years of dedicated research and development and innovation, we have established a
comprehensive electronic test and measurement offering built on two pillars: (i) a
core-technology-driven product matrix, encompassing digital oscilloscopes, microwave and radio
frequency (“RF”, the range of electromagnetic frequencies used for wireless communication)
instruments, direct current (“DC”, the flow of electric charge in a constant direction) and precision
instruments, and modular instruments, and (ii) a suite of customized multi-scenario solutions that
integrate electronic test and measurement instruments with proprietary software, system integration
capabilities and professional services, primarily serving high-growth industries including
communications, new energy, semiconductors, and education and research.
Our commitment to technological innovation has established us as one of the few companies in
the PRC with full-stack, proprietary technology innovation capabilities in the electronic test and
measurementinstrument industry,according to Frost &Sullivan.Through sustained investmentand
continuous advancement, we have built a self-developed and scalable technology platform
integrating hardware, software and algorithms that improves customer efficiency and accelerates
innovation.
MARKET OPPORTUNITIES
Theglobalmarketofelectronictestandmeasurementinstrumentsandsolutionsisexperiencing
robust growth, propelled by rapid technological advancements such as 5G, 6G and optical
communications, artificial intelligence and intelligent robotics. As electronic devices and systems
become increasingly complex, there is a heightened need for high-speed, multi-functional,
high-precision test and measurement solutions to ensure performance, safety and regulatory
compliance. According to Frost & Sullivan, the global market size of electronic test and
measurement instruments and solutions achieved over RMB110 billion in 2025 and is expected to
maintain strong momentum, with a projected CAGR of 9.6% to reach approximately RMB180
billion in 2030.

=== PAGE 11 ===
SUMMARY
Our products and solutions primarily serve the following end markets: communications, new
energy,semiconductors,andeducationandresearch.Theseendmarketsarelarge,diverseandpoised
for growth from sustained tailwinds in electrification and digitization, which we expect to further
propelourgrowth.Theincreasingdemandfortestandmeasurementinstrumentsacrossthesesectors
positiontestandmeasurementcompanies,includingus,tocapturesubstantialgrowthacrossabroad
spectrum of downstream markets.
OUR PRODUCTS AND SOLUTIONS
Weofferawiderangeoftestandmeasurementtoolsdesignedtohelpengineersandresearchers
observe, measure and analyze electrical signals. Our product portfolio includes three categories of
standardized products, comprising (i) digital oscilloscopes, which act like an “engineer’s eye” by
displaying how electrical signals change over time, making it easier to measure, diagnose and
troubleshoot electronic devices, (ii) microwave and RF instruments, which are used to generate and
analyze high-frequency signals, essential for wireless communications technologies, (iii) DC and
precision instruments, such as waveform generators, DC power supplies and digital multimeters,
which allow for source, accurate measurement and control of electrical signals like voltage and
current, as well as (iv) modular instruments, which can be customized and combined to create
flexible testing systems, ideal for complex tasks like automated production testing and scientific
experiments. Beyond general-purpose instruments, we offer flexible, one-stop test and measurement
solutions tailored to the needs of various industries.
OUR CORE TECHNOLOGIES
With over two decades of dedicated research and development, we have established a vertically
integrated technology platform and developed significant in-house capabilities across our electronic
test and measurement instruments and solutions:
. Hardware Architecture: Our hardware strategy is to build on three core pillars: (i) our
proprietary Application Specific Integrated Circuits (“ASICs”, integrated circuits
designed for specific purposes) technology platforms, which form the foundation of our
products’ core competency; (ii) standardized interfaces, which facilitate the rapid
development of new instruments by allowing the combination and configuration of
existing modules, rather than initiating each design from scratch; and (iii) a Common
Building Blocks approach, which provides exceptional scalability and efficiency, allowing
us to quickly develop not only traditional benchtop instruments but also complex,
industry-specific solutions.
. Software Architecture: We have adopted a unified and layered software architecture
specifically designed to maximize reusability and accelerate the pace of development,
which comprises the RIGOL Operating System as the base, with standardized middleware
and drivers layered on top. The entire architecture is completed by a unified application
framework, which incorporates a common user interface library to ensure a consistent
user experience across all products.
. Algorithms: Algorithms serve as the “brain” of our technology system. Our approach to
algorithm development focuses on three key areas: (i) hardware level algorithms, which
enableustooptimizedesignsandidentifypotentialrisksearlyinthedevelopmentprocess,
before physical prototypes are produced; (ii) product level algorithms, which help ensure
superior accuracy and stability of generated signals; and (iii) application level algorithms,
which convert high-fidelity data into meaningful insights for users, addressing specific
challenges.

We believe the following strengths position us well to capitalize on future industry
opportunities and achieve sustained growth:
. Competitive player in the PRC electronic test and measurement industry, bridging
product gaps and shaping industry standards;

OUR STRATEGIES
We plan to pursue the following strategies:
. Build customer-centric global sales, marketing and service networks for sustainable

. Strengthen global supply chain with enhanced manufacturing intelligence and excellence;
. Globalized approach to R&D for next-generation products and solutions; and
. Explore global strategic investments and acquisitions opportunities to solidify market

SALES AND MARKETING
We have established multiple sales channels which include distributor sales and direct sales to
effectively serve a diverse range of customers. We strategically collaborate with distributors who
possess extensive sales channels to expand our market reach and effectively serve the needs of
customersinvariousregions.See“Business—DistributorSales”formoredetails.Inourdirectsales
model, we have a comprehensive key account and online sales network in the Chinese mainland and
overseas markets. Key account sales are primarily direct sales to enterprise customers who purchase
our high-performance products or high value customers. Direct online sales include (i) sales to end
customers through stores we operate on third-party online platforms, (ii) sales to end customers
through our own official website, and (iii) sales to an E-commerce platform customer.
PRODUCTION AND R&D CAPABILITIES
We have developed a manufacturing framework that strategically integrates global and
domestic resources primarily through in-house production. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we
had one production facility in Suzhou and one production facility in Penang, with a total GFA of
14,587.04 sq.m., which enable us to efficiently serve customers in our target markets worldwide.
Furthermore, we have established a R&D network with four R&D centers in Suzhou, Beijing,
Shanghai and Xi’an in the PRC, and one R&D center in Malaysia. Our domestic R&D centers
primarily focus on R&D projects for advancing key technologies such as high-performance digital
oscilloscopes, high-frequency microwave and RF technology and wireless communication protocol
analysis. Our Malaysia R&D center primarily engages in research into the development of hardware
modules, solutions, and localized product improvements. As of December 31, 2025, we maintained a
R&D team of 327 personnel, with approximately 52.3% of our R&D personnel held a master’s or
doctoral degree.
OUR CUSTOMERS AND SUPPLIERS
During the Track Record Period, our customers are primarily distributors, and to a lesser
extent, we sell directly to end customers. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue contributed from our five
largest customers in each year of the Track Record Period accounted for 31.9%, 30.4% and 30.6%
of our total revenue, respectively. Revenue from our largest customer in each year of the Track
Record Period accounted for 11.3%, 10.3% and 12.5% of our total revenue, respectively. See
“Business — Our Customers” for more details. During the Track Record Period, our suppliers
primarily are suppliers in the global mechanical and electronic industry. The major raw materials
supplied by our suppliers mainly include IC chips, electronic components, structural parts, PCBs,

COMPETITION
The electronic test and measurement instrument and solution industry in which we operate is
competitive and evolving with technological innovations, changes in customer demands and
preferences, frequent introduction of new products and application fields. We face intense
competition with global leading players in various aspects of our business, including technology
capability, product design, manufacture and consumer experience. Staying aligned with evolving
industry trends and customer expectations is crucial. By proactively focusing on R&D and
customer-centric product and solution innovations, we believe we are well-positioned to strengthen
our market leadership. Benefitting from the growth potential of electronic test and measurement
instrument and solution market, we believe our well-established brand and global presence,
high-quality and diverse products and solutions, proprietary and advanced technology, efficient
supply chain management, and streamlined manufacturing capabilities, will enable us to grasp the
global market potential and achieve continuous growth. For further details, please refer to the
section headed “Industry Overview.”
RISK FACTORS
Our business and the Global Offering involve certain risks, which are set out in the section
headed “Risk Factors.” You should read that section in its entirety carefully before you decide to
invest in our Shares. Some of the major risks we face include: (i) The markets for our products and
solutionsareevolving,andchangingmarketconditions,suchasintroductionofnewtechnologies,or
changes in customer preferences may negatively affect demand for our products and solutions. If we
fail to properly anticipate or respond to changing market conditions, our business prospects and
resultsofoperationswillsuffer;(ii)Ouroperatinghistorymaynotbeindicativeofourprospectsand
future results of operations; (iii) We face competition and expect competition to increase in the
future. If we fail to compete effectively, our revenue growth and results of operations will be
materially and adversely affected; (iv) We are exposed to risks associated with our global presence
and will continue to be subject to such risks when we further expand our business overseas; (v) We
may be unable to match production with customer demand for a variety of reasons including our
inability to accurately forecastcustomer demand, which could adversely affectour operating results;
(vi) Our growth is affected by the growth and development of the markets served by our customers.
If the underlying market does not develop as we expect, our business prospects may be harmed; (vii)
We have been investing, and intend to continue to invest, heavily in our R&D but such investments
may not yield the results we expect; (viii) A fluctuation in prices of raw materials may disrupt our
supply chain and affect our selling prices, which could affect our business, financial condition and
results of operations; (ix) If we fail to acquire new customers or retain existing customers, our
business, financial condition and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected; and
(x) The complexity of our products may lead to errors, defects and bugs, and we may be subject to
warranty, product recalls or product liability claims, which could negatively impact our reputation
with customers and result in legal liabilities.

Non-IFRS Financial Measures
To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are presented in accordance with
IFRS, we also use adjusted net profit (Non-IFRS Measure) and adjusted EBITDA (Non-IFRS
Measure) as additional financial measures, which are not required by, or presented in accordance
with IFRS. We believe these non-IFRS measures facilitate comparisons of operating performance
from year to year and company to company by eliminating potential impacts of certain items. We
believe these measures provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and
evaluating our combined results of operations in the same manner as they help our management.
However, such non-IFRS financialmeasureswe presented may notbe directly comparable to similar
measures presented by other companies. The use of these non-IFRS measures should not be
considered as substitute for analysis of, our results of operations or financial condition as reported
under IFRS.

losses from RMB48.0 million in 2024 to RMB54.4 million in 2025 primarily due to net foreign
exchange gains.

amortization, attributable to increases in R&D personnel and R&D projects.

SUMMARY
Revenue
Ourrevenueincreasedby38.0%fromRMB167.8millionforthethreemonthsendedMarch31,
2025 to RMB231.6 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, mainly due to (i) an increase
in revenue from modular instruments as our key account customers increased purchases for their
R&Dinitiatives;and(ii)anincreaseinrevenuefromdigitaloscilloscopesdrivenbyincreasedsalesof
our high-end and high-value added products.
Cost of Sales
Our cost of sales increased by 29.8% from RMB79.4 million for the three months ended March
31, 2025 to RMB103.0 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, generally in line with the
growth of our revenue.
Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
Our gross profit increased by 45.3% from RMB88.5 million for the three months ended March
31, 2025 to RMB128.6 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, and our gross profit
margin grew slightly from 52.7% for the three months ended March 31, 2025 to 55.5% for the three
months ended March 31, 2026.
Other Gains and Losses
Our net gains under the item of other gains and losses decreased by 86.5% from RMB16.9
million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 to RMB2.3 million for the three months ended
March 31, 2026. As a percentage of revenue, our net gains under the item of other gains and losses
decreased from 10.1% for the three months ended March 31, 2025 to 1.0% for the three months
ended March 31, 2026. This is mainly due to net foreign exchange losses and decreased gains on fair
value changes of financial assets at FVTPL.
Profit for the Period
As a result of the foregoing, our profit for the period increased by 511.9% from RMB3.8
million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 to RMB23.2 million for the three months ended
March 31, 2026. As a percentage of our revenue, our profit for the period increased from 2.3% for
the three months ended March 31, 2025 to 10.0% for the three months ended March 31, 2026.
Assets and Liabilities
Our total assets remained relatively stable at RMB3,584.6 million as of December 31, 2025 and
RMB3,551.0 million as of March 31, 2026. Our total liabilities decreased by 12.4% from RMB423.8
million as of December 31, 2025 to RMB371.4 million as of March 31, 2026, primarily due to
decreases in our borrowings as well as trade and other payables as we settled these amounts.
Cash Flows
We recorded net cash used in operating activities of RMB5.3 million, net cash from investing
activities of RMB17.9 million and net cash used in financing activities of RMB41.8 million for the
three months ended March 31, 2026.

This glossary of technical terms contains explanations of certain technical terms used in this
prospectus in connection with our Company and our business. Such terminology and meanings may
not correspond to standard industry meanings or usages of those terms.
“A” ampere, a unit of current used to measure the flow of electric charge
“ADC” analog-to-digital converter, a device that converts a continuous analog
signal into a discrete digital signal
“AFG” arbitrary function generator, a signal source that can create standard
arbitrary and function waveforms, allowing users to define precise
parameters like frequency, amplitude, and phase for testing and circuit
stimulus
“AGVs” automated guided vehicles, driverless vehicles capable of using various
navigation technologies and autonomously following predetermined
routes to perform tasks such as material handling, loading, unloading,
and delivery, thereby improving automation and operational efficiency
while reducing the need for manual labor
“AM” amplitude modulation, a technique used in electronic communication
for transmitting information via a radio carrier wave
“ASIC” application-specific integrated circuit, an integrated circuit designed
for specific purposes
“AWG” arbitrary waveform generator, a signal source that can create custom
waveforms defined by the user, enabling precise control over
parameters such as waveform shape, frequency, amplitude, and phase
“bandwidth” the range of frequencies within a given band that a transmission
medium can carry. In the context of data communication, bandwidth is
often used to describe the data transfer rate or capacity of a network,
indicating the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a
networkconnectionin agivenamountoftime,usuallymeasuredin bits
per second (bps)
“bit” a basic unit of data in computing and digital communications. It can
have a value of either 0 or 1, representing the two binary states
“CAGR” compound annual growth rate
“CE certification” Conformite´ Europe´enne certification, which indicates that a product
meets the European Union’s health, safety, and environmental
protection standards. The CE marking is required for certain
products sold within the European Economic Area (EEA) and is also
recognized in other markets. It ensures that the product can be legally
sold and used in the EEA
“Common Building standardized components that can be used interchangeably across
Blocks” different systems or projects. These components serve as the
fundamental parts or units that can be combined in various ways to
create more complex structures or systems, allowing for efficiency,
compatibility, and ease of assembly or integration

RISKS RELATING TO OUR BUSINESS AND OUR INDUSTRY
The markets for our products and solutions are evolving, and changing market conditions, such as
introduction of new technologies, or changes in customer preferences may negatively affect demand for
our products and solutions. If we fail to properly anticipate or respond to changing market conditions,
our business prospects and results of operations will suffer.
The electronic test and measurement instrument and solution industry is subject to constant
changes in technology, product and technology upgrade, frequent new product and solution
introductions and evolving technical standards. New technologies may be introduced that make the
currenttechnologiesonwhichourproductsandsolutionsarebasedlesscompetitiveorevenobsolete
or require us to make changes to our technology that could be expensive and time-consuming to
implement. Due to the evolving nature of our markets, our future success depends on our ability to
accurately anticipate and respond to changes in industry standards, technological requirements,
customer preferences and other market conditions. Our technologies could also become obsolete
sooner than we expect because of faster than anticipated, or unexpected, changes in one or more of
the industry standards and technological requirements. In addition, we may be unable to develop or
introduce new or enhanced technologies that satisfy customer requirements and achieve market
acceptance in a timely manner or at all, succeed in commercializing the technologies on which we
have focused our R&D expenditures to develop, or anticipate new industry standards and
technological changes. If we fail to adapt successfully to technological changes or fail to obtain
access to important new technologies, we may be unable to retain customers or attract new
customers. Any decrease in demand for our products and solutions, due to the emergence of
competing technologies, changes in customer preferences and requirements or otherwise, could
adversely affect our business, results of operations and prospects.
Our operating history may not be indicative of our prospects and future results of operations.
We have experienced growth and expansion since our inception and over the Track Record
Period. Our revenues increased from RMB670.5 million in 2023 to RMB775.8 million in 2024, and
further increased to RMB900.2 million in 2025. We recorded net profits of RMB108.0 million,
RMB92.3 million and RMB86.1 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Our historical results
may not provide a meaningful basis for evaluating our business, results of operations, financial
condition and prospects. We may encounter unforeseen difficulties, complications, delays and other
known and unknown factors, and may not be able to achieve satisfactory results in future periods.
We cannot assure you that we will be able to achieve similar results or grow at the same rates as we
did in the past. Our revenue growth may slow down or even decline in the future for a number of
reasons, including slowing demand for our products and solutions, intensified competition, material
changes in technology, declining growth rate of our total addressable market and our failure to
continue to take advantage of growth opportunities. Our future operating results will depend to a
large extent on our ability to manage our expansion and growth successfully.

On October 28, 2024, the U.S. Department of the Treasury (“Treasury”) issued a final rule,
codified in the United States Code of Federal Regulations at 31 C.F.R. part 850, to implement the
Executive Order 14105 of August 9, 2023 (the “Outbound Investment Rule”), which became effective
onJanuary2,2025.TheOutboundInvestmentRuleimposesinvestmentprohibitionandnotification
requirements on U.S. persons for a wide range of investments in entities associated with China
(including Hong Kong and Macau) that are engaged in activities relating to three sectors: (i)
semiconductors and microelectronics, (ii) quantum information technologies, and (iii) artificial
intelligence systems, collectively defined as “Covered Foreign Persons.” U.S. persons subject to the
OutboundInvestmentRuleareprohibitedfrommaking,orrequiredtoreport,certaininvestmentsin
Covered Foreign Persons, which are defined as “Covered Transactions,” and include certain
acquisitions of an equity interest, certain debt financing, joint ventures, and certain investments as a
limited partner in a non-U.S. person pooled investment fund. The Outbound Investment Rule
contains exceptions for certain investments, including those in publicly traded securities, except
when the U.S. person investor secures rights that go beyond standard minority shareholder
protections. The Outbound Investment Rule may introduce new hurdles and uncertainties for

You should assess the legal protections you are entitled to under legal system in China.
The legal system in China is based on written statutes. Investors should be aware that the
Chinese legal system differs from the common law system in several respects, including its legal
origins and the role of judicial precedents. In addition, like other civil law countries, there is a
limited volume of published court decisions in China, which may be cited for reference but are not
binding on subsequent cases and have limited precedential value unless the Supreme People’s Court
otherwise provides. PRC laws, regulations, judicial interpretations, and regulatory practices may
evolve with economic and social developments, and investors should take this evolving context into
account when assessing the protection of their rights.
In addition, since PRC legislative, judicial, and administrative enforcement authorities have a
certain degree of discretion under law in interpreting and applying statutory provisions and
contractual terms, the outcomes of administrative and judicial proceedings may be subject to
uncertainty. These uncertainties may affect our judgment on the relevance of legal requirements and
our ability to enforce our contractual rights or tort claims. Any litigation or regulatory enforcement
action in China may be protracted and may result in substantial costs and the diversion of resources
and management attention.

WAIVER IN RESPECT OF MANAGEMENT PRESENCE IN HONG KONG
Pursuant to Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules, our Company must have sufficient management
presence in Hong Kong. This normally means that at least two of our executive Directors must be
ordinarily resident in Hong Kong. Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules further provides that
requirement in Rule 8.12 may be waived by having regard to, among other considerations, our
arrangements for maintaining regular communication with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Ourprincipalbusinessoperationsareprimarilylocated,managed,andconductedoutsideHong
KongandwillcontinuetobebasedoutsideHongKong,andourCompany’sheadofficeislocatedin
Suzhou, the PRC. Our executive Directors and senior management members ordinarily reside
outside Hong Kong and play important roles in our Company’s business operations, principally
responsible for the overall management, corporate strategy, planning, business development and
controlofourGroup’sbusiness,itisimportantforthemtoremain incloseproximity totheGroup’s
operations located outside Hong Kong. We consider that it would be practically difficult and
commercially unreasonable for us to arrange for two executive Directors to be ordinarily resident in
Hong Kong, either by relocation of our existing executive Directors or by appointment of additional
executive Directors. For the above reasons, we do not have, and do not contemplate in the

OVERVIEW OF GLOBAL ELECTRONIC TEST AND MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT AND
SOLUTION MARKET
As a strategic, foundational high-tech sector, electronic test and measurement comprises the
instruments and systems that quantify and verify the performance, quality and reliability of
electronic circuits and devices. The industry’s growth is closely aligned with a nation’s industrial
GDP. It serves as indispensable tools for engineers and researchers, supporting the entire product
lifecycle — from R&D and mass production testing to deployment and maintenance — and serving
as a core pillar of technological innovation.
Introduction of Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument and Solution Market
The global market for electronic test and measurement is poised for significant growth.
AccordingtoFrost&Sullivan,themarketisprojectedtogrowfromoverRMB110billionin2025to
approximately RMB180 billion by 2030, representing a CAGR of 9.6% from 2026 to 2030. This
market primarily consists of two core offerings: instruments and solutions.
– 75 –

=== PAGE 85 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Electronic Test and Measurement Instruments
These are the core hardware devices used to measure electrical parameters and signals. These
sophisticated instruments integrate advanced technologies such as digital signal processing,
microelectronics, and complex software to deliver precision and performance. They serve as
foundational tools across a wide range of industries and applications.
Electronic Test and Measurement Solutions
The solutions represent a higher level of integration. They combine instruments with
specialized software, accessories, and technical support to create a comprehensive system. This
holistic approach is designed to address the complex, end-to-end testing challenges of specific
applications and industries, delivering greater value to the customer.
Value Chain of Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument and Solution
The value chain of electronic test and measurement instruments and solutions mainly consists
of upstream suppliers, midstream manufacturers and solution providers, and downstream
applications in various fields:
. Upstream mainly involves suppliers of electronic components and materials,
electromechanical components, mechanical processing and electronic assembly. As a
fundamental unit, ICchips determine the performance of electronic test and measurement
instruments in processing speed and efficiency, proposing stringent technical
requirements.
. Midstream involves manufacturers engaging in R&D, production and sales of electronic
test and measurement instruments and providers of electronic test and measurement
solutions.
. Downstream applications cover fields including communications, new energy,
semiconductors, education and research, and diversified electronics, which propose
stringent requirements on measurement accuracy and reliability.

Drivers of Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument and Solution Market
Thedemand forelectronic testandmeasurementinstruments and solutionsisdirectly fueled by
innovation in key downstream sectors. As these industries evolve, they require more advanced test
and measurement capabilities, creating a sustained growth cycle for the instrument and solution
market.
. Communications: The rollout of 5G/6G, optical communications and the expansion of
high-speed data centers demand instruments capable of validating significantly higher
frequencies and bandwidths. This relentless pursuit of faster data transmission directly
drives the need for high-performance oscilloscopes and RF instruments.
– 76 –

=== PAGE 86 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
. New Energy: The global shift to electrification, especially in electric vehicles (“EVs”) and
renewable energy systems, creates a massive need for electronic test and measurement
instruments and solutions. These are essential for safely and efficiently testing
high-power, high-voltage electronics, from battery management systems to grid-tied
inverters.
. Semiconductors: As chips become more complex, powerful, and integrated into every
aspect of life, the need for precise and automated testing intensifies. Instruments and
solutions are critical at every stage, from initial design validation to high-volume
production, ensuring the quality and reliability of the foundational components of the
digital world.
. Education and Research: This sector provides a stable, foundational demand. Educational
institutions require large volumes of fundamental instruments to train future engineers,
while cutting-edge scientific research constantly pushes the boundaries of measurement,
demanding the most advanced and often customized instruments available.
Entry Barriers of Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument and Solution Market
Threshold of Technical Capabilities
The industry of electronic test and measurement instruments and solutions driven by
multi-disciplinary technologies has extremely high technical barriers. It requires long-term R&D
for companies to build their own patent and technology systems. In the process of
commercialization, stringent requirements are imposed on manufacturing processes in pursuit of
the ultimate performances of bandwidth, dynamic range and processing efficiency, when companies
with R&D capabilities of core components and technologies including hardware, software and
algorithms are more competitive in the market.
Scarcity in Specialized Talents
Electronic test and measurement instruments are complex electronic systems comprised of
hardware, software and algorithms, requiring comprehensive expertise across multiple disciplines
and specialists in technologies of specific fields, planning and integration of system, and practical
applications. A specialist team with experience and talents is key to companies’ competitiveness.
New companies will face the high cost of cultivating a team with strong competitiveness.
Competitiveness Based on Manufacturing, Sales and Service Network
For companies, global footprint is a strategic necessity to achieve market proximity, cost
optimization, and supply chain resilience, which proposes stringent requirements on the capital
investment and operation capability. Customers tend to make comprehensive evaluation of the
brand reputation and service quality of electronic test and measurement instrument and solution
companies to reduce transaction costs and risks, which requires long-term accumulation of
technology, knowledge and management experience in the market practice. Meanwhile, the service
scope of companies widely covers manufacturers in various industries, research institutes,
universities and individual users. A comprehensive network of sales and service is a powerful
means for companies to seize market share and amplify the brand influence, which requires
long-term investment.
OVERVIEW OF ELECTRONIC TEST AND MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT MARKET
Electronic test and measurement instruments are mainly applied in detecting and analyzing of
general electrical parameters including voltage, current and resistance. Electronic test and
measurement instruments are the fundamental equipment of the development of a variety of
industries, covering a wide range of application scenarios.

steady expansion, with a CAGR of 4.8% from 2021 to 2025. In 2025, the global electronic test and

Market Size of China Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument
In recent years, China Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument market has maintained a
faster growth rate than the global average, with a remarkable CAGR of 7.0% from 2021 to 2025. In
2025, China Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument market achieved RMB21.5 billion in
revenue. Looking ahead, the market is projected to maintain strong growth momentum, with an
estimated CAGR of 7.3% from 2026 to 2030. The demand for electronic test and measurement
equipment in China outgrew the global market, driven by the rapid growing demand of downstream
applications including communications, new energy, and semiconductors. In the future, with the
increasing localization rate of semiconductors, the construction of new-generation communication
infrastructure, and the rapid growth of AI computing power, the demand for electronic test and
measurementequipmentin emerging industrieswill continueto lead globally, which directly intrigue
the growth potential of China’s electronic test and measurement equipment market.
In the segmented market, digital oscilloscopes demonstrated the highest growth rate due to
strong downstream demand, achieving a remarkable CAGR of 8.9% from 2021 to 2025. The market
is projected to maintain steady growth with an estimated CAGR of 8.2% during the 2026–2030
period.

Drivers and Trends of Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument Market
Electronic test and measurement products, i.e., the standalone instruments that form the
bedrock of the industry, are primarily driven by the pursuit of higher physical performance and
enhanced tool efficiency. These trends relate directly to the design, functionality, and accessibility of
the instruments themselves.
The Unceasing Demand for Higher Performance
The primary driver for instrument innovation is the relentless push at the physics level by
downstream industries. 6G research demands wider bandwidths and terahertz frequencies; electric
vehicles require testing at higher voltages and power levels; and advanced semiconductors need
instruments with superior sensitivity to measure minuscule signals. This creates a permanent,
high-value upgrade cycle for premium instruments that can operate at the cutting edge of
performance.
– 81 –

=== PAGE 91 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Integration of Multiple Functions into a Single Platform
To enhance efficiency and save valuable lab space, there is a strong trend towards
multi-function instruments. Modern oscilloscopes, for instance, frequently integrate the
capabilities of spectrum analyzers, logic analyzers, and protocol decoders into one platform. This
consolidation improves workflow for engineers, reduces capital expenditure for lab managers, and
makes powerful testing capabilities more accessible.
Adoption of Modular and Scalable Architectures
There is a growing adoption of modular product architectures, both in hardware and software.
Hardware platforms like PCI eXtensions for Instrumentation Express (PXIe) allow users to create
customized, high-density test systems by combining instrument modules in a single chassis, which is
the physical framework or structure that houses and supports the internal components of a device.
This offers superior scalability and a smaller footprint for automated applications. Concurrently,
standalone instruments are increasingly designed as software-upgradable platforms, enabling users
to unlock features or higher performance via licenses, thus protecting their initial hardware
investment.
Accelerated Market Share Gain by PRC Companies
A notable industry trend is the growing competitiveness of PRC companies. Through
significant, long-term investment in R&D, these companies have substantially narrowed the
product performance gap with global market leaders. Leveraging the scale and rapid innovation
cycles of the PRC high-tech industry, they are increasingly winning market share, not only in
domestic market but also by expanding into the global high-performance product segment.
OVERVIEW OF ELECTRONIC TEST AND MEASUREMENT SOLUTION MARKET
Introduction of Electronic Test and Measurement Solution Market
Electronic test and measurement solutions refer to solutions focusing on industry-purpose
electronic test and measurement demands. It delivers integrated electronic test and measurement
systems and industry-specific instruments, encompassing devices, accessories, software and technical
supports. Electronic test and measurement solutions can accurately address demands in specific
fields including communications, new energy, semiconductors, education and research.
With the development of electronic test and measurement requirements, single function
measurement instruments are increasingly unable to satisfy the diversified demands of downstream
customers. By encapsulating multiple measurement functions and modularizing based on specific
needs, electronic test and measurement solutions can better satisfy the operational, technical and
application demands of various industries, improving the overall efficiency. Electrification of
mobility, DC factories, connected homes, smart buildings, and digital health is creating a need for
high performance electronics, which has resulted in new sustained demand for electronic test and
measurement solutions in order to ensure the performance, reliability and safety of these electronic
components and systems.
Market Size of Global Electronic Test and Measurement Solution
In recent years, electronic test and measurement solution market has experienced rapid
expansion, with a CAGR of 12.9% in global scale from 2021 to 2025. In 2025, the global electronic
test and measurement solution market achieved RMB55.6 billion in revenue. Looking ahead, the
market is projected to maintain strong growth momentum, with an estimated CAGR of 13.8% in
global scale from 2026 to 2030.

Drivers and Trends of Electronic Test and Measurement Solution Market
The drivers for the solution market transcend the hardware itself, focusing on solving
higher-level challenges customers face in system integration, engineering efficiency, and business
success. These trends reflect the strategic evolution of the test provider’s role.
Acceleration of Time-to-Market through Turnkey Systems
In hyper-competitive industries, reducing the product development cycle is a critical business
imperative. Customers increasingly demand turnkey solutions that are ready to deploy, eliminating
the months of R&D effort required to build and debug a custom test system. By providing a
validated platform with application-specific software, electronic test and measurement solutions
directly accelerate a customer’s journey from design to market.
Demand for Standardized and Scalable Automation Frameworks
To ensure quality and consistency from R&D to production, companies need standardized and
scalable test frameworks. Solutions address this by providing a unified software platform that can
automate testing across the entire product lifecycle. This industrialization of the test process is
critical for achieving high-throughput manufacturing and ensuring product reliability at scale.
– 84 –

=== PAGE 94 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Evolution from Product Vendor to Solution Partner
Solving system-level challenges requires deep application expertise that goes far beyond the
instrument itself. Customers are seeking partners, not just suppliers, who understand their specific
industry and can deliver a complete, outcome-focused solution. This trend is shifting the business
model towards long-term, service-intensive partnerships built on solution expertise.
The Historical Producer Price Index for The Computer, Communications and Other Electronic
Equipment Manufacturing Industry
The raw materials and parts of the Company’s electronic test and measurement instruments
and solutions include various electronic components and equipment, including IC chips, PCBs and
displays, etc. The Producer Price Index (“PPI”) for the computer, communications and other
electronic components and equipment manufacturing industry is the composite price index released
by the National Bureau of Statistics including the electronic components and equipment as above. It
reflects the price trend of the raw materials and parts of the Company.
From 2020 to 2022, driven by factors such as the growth in demand from downstream sectors
and technological iteration and upgrading, the PPI of this industry rose from 98.5 to 100.7, and the
prices of raw materials showed an upward trend. After 2022, with the gradual expansion of industry
capacity and intensified market competition, the PPI fell to 97.6 in 2024, and the prices of raw
materials declined accordingly. The full-year based statistical data of the PPI has not yet been
publiclyreleasedbytheNationalBureauofStatistics.Comparedwiththemonthlyyear-on-yeardata
of 2024, the PPI experienced a slight decline in the first half of 2025, under the background of the
robust production capacity and gradually rose in the second half of the year, driven by the
manufacturing demand in AI-related industries. Overall, the PPI in 2025 is expected to show a slight
downward trend compared to 2024. Among the PPI, the market price of memory chips have risen in
2025 due to the increasing demand for high-performance products and periodic shortage of supply.
In 2026, as AI further drives the demand forthe related electronicmanufacturing industry chain and
combined with the trend of sustained capacity release, the PPI is expected to remain stable or
experienceaslightrebound.In2026,themarketpriceofmemorychipsisexpectedtograduallyenter
a stable stage, with the release of production capacity and return to market supply-demand balance.
In the long run, although the continuous innovation of downstream technologies will stimulate new
demand for raw materials, the increasingly improved global capacity layout and sufficient market
competition will drive the prices of raw materials to stabilize.

We take into account the changes in the major raw material prices for our product pricing.

changes in the major raw material is one of the factors affecting the historical selling price of the
Group’s final products, such as fluctuation of IC chips including ASIC and FPGA. Moreover, the
selling price of the Group’s final products is affected by multiple factors, including types of
customers, selling scales and business arrangement. The major customers of the Group’s products
are mainly to-B customers, including manufacturing enterprises in communication, new energy and
semiconductors, which have relatively high cost-sensitivity. The selling price is determined by selling
scales and specific business arrangement and strategy.

5. Post-A Share Listing Increases in Registered Capital
On April 25, 2023, our then shareholders resolved to increase our registered capital by
undergoing a capital reserve conversion and issuing an additional 4.8 A Shares per 10 A Shares held
by existing shareholders, resulting in the additional issuance of 58,228,586 A Shares. Following the
completion of the capital conversion, our registered capital was 179,538,140 A Shares.
On June 20, 2023, we granted a total of 284,600 restricted A share units to qualified employees,
resulting in a further increase in our registered capital to 179,822,740 A Shares.
As approved by the then shareholders in April 2023 and the CSRC in September 2023, our
Company conducted a private placement of its A Shares to raise funds for various development
initiatives, including the construction of our R&D and production base in Malaysia as well as R&D
center in Xi’an. A total of 5,300,676 A Shares were issued in the placement to 12 investors, all of
whom were Independent Third Parties. The placement raised net proceeds of approximately
RMB290.00 million. Following the completion of the private placement, the Company’s total issued
share capital increased to 185,123,416 A Shares.
On August 30, 2024, we completed the additional share issuance of 7,098,837 A Shares to fund
the acquisition of the Naishu Electronics Group. Following the additional share issuance, our
registered share capital was 192,222,253 A Shares.
As approved by the then shareholders in April 2024 and the CSRC in July 2024, our Company
conducted a private placement of its A Shares to raise funds to fund the construction of our Beijing
laboratory. A total of 2,166,377 A Shares were issued in the placement to 5 investors, all of whom
were Independent Third Parties. The placement raised net proceeds of approximately RMB50.00
million.Followingthecompletionoftheprivateplacement,theCompany’stotalissuedsharecapital
increased to 194,388,630 A Shares.
On October 29, 2024, we repurchased and cancelled 284,600 restricted A share units granted to
certain grantees due to failure to achieve vesting conditions and resignation of certain grantees,
resulting in our registered share capital becoming 194,104,030 A shares.
On November 25 2025, we repurchased and cancelled 229,613 restricted A share units granted
to certain grantees due to failure to achieve vesting conditions and resignation of certain grantees,
resulting in our registered share capital becoming 193,874,417 A shares.

PUBLIC FLOAT
Rules 8.08 and 19A.13A of the Listing Rules require that there must be an open market in the
securities for which listing is sought. Where a new applicant is a PRC issuer with other listed shares
at the time of listing, this will normally mean that the portion of H shares for which listing is sought
that are held by the public, at the time of listing, must: (a) represent at least 10% of the issuer’s total
numberofissuedsharesintheclasstowhichHsharesbelong(excludingtreasuryshares);or(b)have
an expected market value of not less than HK$3,000,000,000.
To the best knowledge and belief of our Directors and on the basis of the current shareholding
structure, none of the H Shares is expected to be held by our core connected person and the
24,802,200 H Shares to be issued under the Global Offering is expected to represent approximately
11.34% of our total issued share capital immediately following completion of the Global Offering
(assuming no other changes are made to the issued share capital of our Company between the Latest
Practicable Date and the Listing) will be counted towards the public float, which exceeds the
minimum prescribed public float percentage under Rule 19A.13A(2)(a) of the Listing Rules. Based
on the above, it is expected that our Company will be able to comply with the public float
requirement under Rule 19A.13A(2) of the Listing Rules at the time of Listing.
FREE FLOAT
Rule 19A.13C(2)ofthe Listing Rulesprovides that, where anewapplicantisa PRCissuerwith
other listed shares at the time of listing, this will normally mean that the portion of H shares for
which listing is sought that are held by the public and not subject to any disposal restrictions
(whetherundercontract,theListingRules,applicablelawsorotherwise),atthetimeoflisting,must:
(a)representatleast5%ofthetotalnumberofissued sharesintheclassto which Hsharesbelongat
the time of listing (excluding treasury shares), with an expected market value at the time of listing of
not less than HK$50,000,000; or (b) have an expected market value at the time of listing of not less
than HK$600,000,000. Our Company will satisfy the free float requirement under Rule 19A.13C(2)
of the Listing Rules.

BUSINESS
OVERVIEW
We are an electronic test and measurement instrument company in the PRC with advanced
technology capabilities and extensive global footprint. According to Frost & Sullivan, we are the
largest PRC electronic test and measurement instrument provider and ranked eighth globally in
terms of revenue in 2025. We design, develop, manufacture and deliver a comprehensive suite of
electronic test and measurement instruments and solutions that power scientific discovery and
industrial innovation. Under the “RIGOL” brand, we serve a diverse customer base of over 100,000
end customers across more than 90 countries and regions, addressing complex test challenges across
communications, new energy, semiconductors, and education and research sectors. We are
committed to innovation and in-house mastery of core technologies. Through sustained advances
in hardware, software and algorithms, we have built a proprietary core technology platform and
established ourselves as a competitive electronic test and measurement enterprise.
At RIGOL, we believe that “science begins with measurement.” Electronic test and
measurement instruments are devices designed for observing, testing, measuring and calculating a
wide range of physical parameters. These instruments offer capabilities such as detection and
measurement, signal transmission and data processing, and can be used to diagnose, test and verify
the performance of other electronic devices or components. Electronic test and measurement
instruments are fundamental to the advancement of modern science and technology. Through years
of dedicated research and development and innovation, we have established a comprehensive
electronic test and measurement offering built on two pillars: (i) a core-technology-driven product
matrix, encompassing digital oscilloscopes, microwave and RF instruments, DC and precision
instruments, and modular instruments, and (ii) a suite of multi-scenario solutions, primarily serving
high-growth industries including communications, new energy, semiconductors, and education and
research. According to Frost & Sullivan,
. We are the largest PRC digital oscilloscope provider and ranked fifth globally in terms of
revenue in 2025;
. We are the largest PRC waveform generators provider and ranked third globally in terms
of revenue in 2025; and
. We are the first and only PRC company to have successfully commercialized digital
oscilloscopes with self-developed ASICs.
Our global sales and service network spans the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific. According
to Frost & Sullivan, we led PRC companies in terms of overseas revenue from electronic test and
measurement instruments in 2025. Supported by our proprietary core technologies, we help
customers overcome complex testing challenges to achieve sustainable, long-term growth in the
global electronic test and measurement market. As of December 31, 2025, among the companies on
the 2025 Fortune Global 500 list, we had served:
. 100% of the computer and office equipment companies;
. 93% of the electronics and electrical equipment companies;
. 83% of the semiconductor and other electronic components companies;
. 100% of the telecommunication companies; and
. 77% of the motor vehicles and parts companies.
. 87 of the world’s top 100 universities (QS World University Rankings) utilized
RIGOL-branded products, as of the same date.

BUSINESS
Although we recorded a decrease in our gross profit margin from 2024 to 2025, it was mainly
due to (i) the production capacity ramp-up of our Penang Production Center in Malaysia, which led
to relatively lower cost efficiency; (ii) increased raw material and component costs, which cannot be
fully passed on to customers through price adjustments in the short term; (iii) a more competitive
pricing strategy for certain digital oscilloscopes and DC and precision instruments products in
responsetointensifiedmarketcompetitionandtoexpandmarketshare,whichledtoslightdecreases
in the average selling price of such products from 2024 to 2025; and (iv) the relatively lower gross
profit margin related to provision of solutions to customers in the education sector, mainly due to a
large and complex project which involved a high portion of procured third-party hardware, software
and services leading to higher costs.
We plan to improve our profitability going forward primarily through (i) normalized and
optimized operations of our Penang Production Center following its production capacity ramp-up,
including (a) optimizing the product mix by introducing more high-margin product lines; (b)
localizingtherawmaterialprocurementtoenablecostsaving;(c)enhancingsellingeffortstoexpand
overseas markets and facilitate order acquisition so as to improve production capacity utilization
rate and reduce per-unit manufacturing costs; and (d) improving the production process, including
targeted production process optimization and on-site employee training programs; the production
capacity ramp-up of our Penang Production Center has achieved significant progress, whose
production capacity utilization rate has risen from less than 40% at its early ramp-up stage to over
80% as of March 31, 2026; (ii) enhancing in-house technological capabilities, particularly our
self-developed ASIC capabilities, to improve cost control efficiency and expand high-end product
portfolio; our self-developed ASICs may empower our cost control specifically by (a) reducing our
demand for off-the-shelf components and materials which are less cost efficient, as our ASICs are
highly integrated; for example, the material and surface mount costs of our certain signal processing
modules, which were equipped with highly integrated ASICs in September 2024, decreased by over
50%comparedwithsuchcostswithouthighlyintegratedASICs;(b)eliminatingredundantfunctions
and transistors with a highly tailored design to serve our products, thereby lowering manufacturing
costs; and (c) enabling us to develop high-end products with relatively higher margins and lower
costs; and (iii) mitigating raw material price volatility through strategic inventory management,
particularly by establishing buffer stock levels for key materials.
Market Opportunities
The global market of test and measurement instruments and solutions witness increased
demand driven by the rollout of 5G, 6G and optical communications, the proliferation of AI chips
and data centers, and the rise of intelligent robots. As electronic devices and systems become more
complex, there is a heightened need for high-speed, multi-functional, high-precision test and
measurementsolutionstoensureperformance,safetyandregulatorycompliance.AccordingtoFrost
& Sullivan, the global market size of electronic test and measurement instruments and solutions in
2025 achieved over RMB110 billion. Looking ahead, the market is projected to maintain strong
growth momentum, with an estimated CAGR of 9.6% from 2026 to 2030, reaching approximately
RMB180 billion in 2030.
Our products and solutions primarily serve the following end markets: communications, new
energy,semiconductors,andeducationandresearch.Theseendmarketsarelarge,diverseandpoised
for growth from sustained tailwinds in electrification and digitization, which we expect to further
propel our growth. More specifically, according to Frost & Sullivan:
Communications
In the communications sector, the deep integration of 5G and optical communications
technologies has become a major industry trend. The large-scale commercialization of 5G is driving
substantial demand for testing to verify the performance and stability of networks and
infrastructure, fueling a surge in the demand for electronic test and measurement instruments and
solutions. Moreover, advances toward 5G and 6G are pushing data transmission frequencies higher

with lower latency, increasing requirements for digital oscilloscopes and microwave and RF
instruments — particularly high bandwidth, sampling rate and frequency range — to support
high-speed signal processing and analysis.
New Energy
The new energy sector, including electric vehicles, renewable power generation such as solar,
wind and hydrogen and energy storage, is experiencing rapid expansion driven by global
decarbonization initiatives, government incentives and technological innovation. The proliferation
of distributed energy resources, smart grids, advanced battery technologies and power electronics is
reshaping the energy landscape, creating complex systems that require rigorous validation and
monitoring, thereby generating robust demand for electronic test and measurement instruments and
solutions. With the capability of offering high-precision, multi-functional and automated
instruments and solutions, supporting high-voltage, high-frequency and remote testing
requirements, and addressing grid compliance, battery safety and predictive maintenance, we
believe we are well-positioned to capture growth in this sector.
Semiconductors
In the semiconductor industry, the foundational requirements of automated test system, chip
validation and circuit design create substantial market opportunities for electronic test and
measurement companies. The automated test systems enable fast and accurate testing of logic,
analog and mixed-signal devices, thereby driving demand for digital oscilloscopes, signal generators,
spectrum analyzers and other core test instruments that support functional verification, fault
detection and parametric analysis. As chip applications expand into diverse areas, design houses
require flexible and scalable test solutions to validate new architectures and support rapid
prototyping. As circuit design advances, the need for precise, reliable and efficient testing solutions
becomes critical to ensure product quality, performance and compliance with industry standards.
Leveraging our flexible and scalable test and measurement instruments and solutions, we are well
positioned to seize significant growth opportunities in the semiconductor industry.
Education and Research
The education and research sector presents significant opportunities for electronic test and
measurement instrument and solution provider. The education and research sector is undergoing
transformation as STEM curricula, university laboratories and research institutes increasingly focus
on emerging technologies such as AI, robotics and advanced materials. The push for hands-on,
project-based learning and interdisciplinary research is driving investment in modern laboratory
infrastructure and test equipment. Solutions that combine high performance, modularity and ease of
use while supporting remote access and collaborative workflows are in high demand. With scalable
product and solutions portfolios, we believe we are well-positioned to serve the evolving needs of
academic institutions and research organizations to provide educational support.
Our Products and Solutions
Our product portfolio encompasses digital oscilloscopes, microwave and RF instruments, DC
and precision instruments, and modular instruments.
. Digital Oscilloscopes: Recognized as the “engineer’s eye” and as an indispensable tool for
engineersacross countlessapplications,it is used to observe and analyzeelectricalsignals.
It captures these signals and converts them into digital form, allowing users to visualize
how the signals change overtime on a screen, proving an intuitive way to analyze the
behavior of various electrical signals.
– 102 –

=== PAGE 112 ===
BUSINESS
. Microwave and RF Instruments: These instruments are used for generating, measuring and
analyzing microwave and RF signals and their spectrum, phase, and modulation
characteristics. Three main types of products are (i) transmitting devices like signal
generators;(ii)signalanalysisdeviceslikespectrumandsignalanalyzers;and(iii)network
measurement devices like vector network analyzers.
. DC and Precision Instruments: This product category includes arbitrary function
generator (“AFG”, a signal source that can create standard arbitrary and function
waveforms) and arbitrary waveform generator (“AWG”, a signal source that can create
custom waveforms defined by the user), programmable DC power supplies and DC
electronic loads, digital multimeters and data acquisition (“DAQ”) system. They are
indispensable tools for engineers and researchers in a vast array of applications, used to
precisely source, measure and analyze fundamental electrical parameters like voltage,
current and resistance.
. Modular Instruments: These are flexibly configurable test and measurement equipment
based on a standardized hardware architecture, forming a multi-functional instrument
system by combining different modules. They are typically used to build scalable,
high-channel-count systems that precisely synchronize tasks such as data acquisition,
generation and analysis. In our modular instrument system, users can flexibly combine
modules like digital oscilloscopes, signal generators, and digital multimeters within a
single chassis to create the exact setup they need. These modular instruments are
commonlyusedindemandingapplicationslikeautomatedproductiontest,semiconductor
validation and large-scale physics experiments.
In addition to general-purpose devices, we offer flexible, one-stop test and measurement
solutions that meet the diverse demands of customers across various industry. We primarily serve
leading technology enterprises in the communications, new energy, semiconductors, and education
and research industries.
. Communications: We address the testing requirements for both wired and wireless
communications in application scenarios such as research and development, validation
and production.
. New Energy: Our offerings cater to the electronic system testing needs in sectors such as
renewable power generation, energy storage and electric vehicles.
. Semiconductors: We support the testing needs of automated test systems and throughout
the circuit design, chip development, validation and application cycle.
. Education and Research: We fulfill the comprehensive testing needs from foundational
teaching and laboratory development to advanced scientific research, supporting course
development, researcher innovation, and the exploration of new technologies.

Our Acquisition and Synergies with Naishu Electronics Group
In 2024, we strategically acquired Naishu Electronics Group, a specialist in intelligent digital
array systems. This acquisition helps us shift from providing standalone hardware instrument to
delivering integrated, software-driven test and measurement solutions tailored to customers’ needs.
The acquisition enhances our capabilities across advanced modular instruments and strengthens our
ability to provide scalable solutions. Our synergies are primarily realized through deep integration
and value amplification across products, solutions, R&D systems and market expansion.
For products and solutions, the acquisition accelerates the execution of our modular
instrument strategy. By integrating Naishu Electronics Group’s expertise in multi-channel RF
transceiver module design with our modular platform, we expand our portfolio from individual
instruments to high-performance modular instruments and solutions. Building on this integration,
we launched new modular instruments, SUA8000 and SPQ platforms, in 2025, reinforcing our
position in automated test system integration. In R&D and production, our technology stacks are
highly complementary. By combining our strengths in high-speed data acquisition, proprietary
ASICs and precision components with Naishu Electronics Group’s capabilities in large-scale
multi-channel synchronization, digital signal processing and complex system integration, we can
break through design limits and develop complex, high-integration test systems tailored to industry
applications.Inparticular,NaishuElectronicsGroup’sextensivehardwaredesignIPandspecialized
algorithm libraries will enrich the firmware of our standard instruments, enhancing
application-specific analytics and competitiveness. Collectively, these synergies shorten
development cycles, reduce costs and time-to-market, deepen our product and solution
capabilities and accelerate platform innovation, reinforcing our competitive advantage in modular
instruments and solutions.

Digital Oscilloscopes
Our core product, digital oscilloscopes, are instruments used to observe and analyze electrical
signals. They capture these signals and convert them into digital waveform, allowing users to
visualize how the signals change over time on a screen, providing an intuitive way to analyze the
behavior of various electrical signals. The performance of digital oscilloscopes is mainly determined
by bandwidth, which indicates the range of signal frequencies the device can detect. Other important
features include howfast the oscilloscopes can sample signals (sampling rate), the speed at which the
oscilloscopes can update the waveform display (waveform refresh rate), the maximum number of
data points that the oscilloscopes can capture (memory depth), and the precision of signal
measurement (vertical resolution). Leveraging our proprietary ASICs, our digital oscilloscope
DS80000, is a pioneering product achieving a maximum analog bandwidth of 13 GHz, a peak
real-time sampling rate of 40 GSa/s, and a maximum memory depth of 4 Gpts, which demonstrates
our competitive advantage in the industry in the PRC, according to Frost & Sullivan.

leadership among PRC enterprises in core technical metrics, including analog bandwidth,

Microwave and RF Instruments
OurmicrowaveandRF instrumentsareessentialtoolsforgenerating,measuringandanalyzing
frequency electromagnetic signals. These tools are designed to handle wireless signals, which range
from 3 kHz to 300 GHz and are used in short to medium-range (i) RF communications like
broadcasting and walkie-talkies; and (ii) microwave signals, which typically range from 300 MHz to
300 GHz, and are ideal for high-speed data transmission in technologies like 5G and satellite
communications.Theseinstrumentsallowuserstomeasure and analyze signalswith precision across
frequency domains, which refer to the rate at which a signal oscillates.
We offer three main types of microwave and RF instruments, categorized based on their
functions: (i) transmitting devices, like signal generators; (ii) signal analysis devices, like spectrum
and signal analyzers; and (iii) network measurement devices, like vector network analyzers.
. Signal Generators: Our signal generators are used to create precise electromagnetic signals
for test engineering and development purposes. They integrate advanced technologies to
ensure precise amplitude control and support functions like pulse modulation, IQ
modulation, and power meter measurement software.
. Spectrum/Signal Analyzers: Our spectrum and signal analyzers are versatile tools that
display the frequency characteristics of signals, facilitating accurate measurement of
aspects such as signal distortion, modulation and stability. Our signal analyzer includes
both entry-level and high-performance series, supporting various operational functions
such as general and real-time spectrum analysis, vector signal and network analysis,
analog demodulation, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) pre-compatibility test.
– 113 –

BUSINESS
. Vector Network Analyzers: Our vector network analyzers are precision instruments used
to measure the transmission and reflection characteristics of electronic components,
circuits and systems in high-frequency environments. By accurately capturing key
parameters such as insertion loss, return loss, phase and impedance, these analyzers
enable users to evaluate the performance of devices including filters, amplifiers, antennas
and cables.

DC and Precision Instruments
Our DC and precision instruments deliver precision measurement and power solutions for
R&D, validation and production. This product category encompasses waveform generators, DC
power supplies, DC electronic loads, high-precision digital multimeters, and DAQ system. Our DC
andprecisioninstrumentsareengineeredtomeetstringentdemandsincommunications,newenergy,
semiconductorsandeducationandresearchapplications.Leveragingproprietarysignalconditioning
algorithms and self-calibration technologies, these instruments ensure lab-grade accuracy, stability,
and repeatability across dynamic test and measurement environments.
. Waveform Generators: Our waveform generators create electrical signals with different
frequencies, shapes and strengths. Our offerings include both AFG and AWG, known for
their stable performance and high quality. AFG can produce arbitrary standard signal
shapes like sine and square waves, while AWG can create complex, custom signal shapes.
Our SiFi® technology platform has enabled us to launch China’s highest performance
5GHz AWG, which competes strongly internationally. According to Frost & Sullivan, we
are the largest PRC waveform generator provider and ranked third globally in terms of
revenue in 2025.

Modular Instruments
Our modular instruments are flexibly configurable test and measurement devices designed
based on standardized hardware architecture. By integrating various functional modules or cards
into a chassis, such as digitizers, signal generators, data acquisition, spectrum analyzers and
controllers, these instruments form a multi-functional instrument system. They support automation
and remote control, significantly boosting testing efficiency while reducing procurement and
maintenance costs. Leveraging their scalability and cost-effectiveness, our modular instruments can
meet the demands of complex testing scenarios such as communications, new energy,
semiconductors, and education and research.

Case Study — High-Precision Optical Time-Domain Reflectometer System Solution
In the fields of fiber optic communications and sensing, the high-precision Optical
Time-Domain Reflectometer (“OTDR”) system is a crucial measurement instrument. We
collaborated with a national high-tech enterprise specializing in fiber optic sensing technology and
IoT application solutions, offering a comprehensive application solution for their R&D testing of
high-precision OTDR systems.
Challenges:
. High-Precision Signal Generation: The development of a high-precision OTDR system
required the generation of complex high-speed pulse sequences with precise control over
laser output.
. High-Resolution Signal Acquisition: The system needed to capture weak backscattered
signals with high accuracy, necessitating high bandwidth and deep storage capabilities.
. System Integration and Optimization: The OTDR system development required seamless
integration and optimization of signal generation and analysis throughout the system
design and testing process.
Our Solutions and Advantages:
Our solution consists of optical source module, optical emission module, optical reception
module and signal processing module, leveraging the collaboration of DG70000 series waveform
generators and DS70000 series digital oscilloscopes. These instruments were seamlessly integrated
through our proprietary software platform, providing customers with a unified control and analysis
environment, which reduce their development complexity and time cost. According to Frost &
Sullivan, our DG70000 series high-performance waveform generators and DS70000 series
high-performance digital oscilloscopes lead the industry in key metrics such as storage depth,
waveform capture rate and vertical resolution. DG70000 series high-performance waveform
generator offers a 12GSa/s sampling rate, 2GHz analog bandwidth and 16-bit vertical resolution.
This ensures the amplitude accuracy and frequency stability of the sweep pulses. Additionally, the
DS70000 series high-performance digital oscilloscopes, with their deep memory, high resolution and
a low-noise front end capacity, were used to capture the time-domain details of weak scattering
signals accurately.
Value Propositions:
In the development of the OTDR system, the collaborative use of the signal generator and
oscilloscope throughout the system design, debugging and optimization processes significantly
improves the OTDR system’s performance. The combination of DG70000 and DS70000, together
with our core modules, significantly enhances the dynamic range, spatial resolution and noise
resistance of the OTDR system, providing key technical support for high-precision fiber optic
sensing and fault diagnosis. Through the application of our comprehensive solution, the customer
has completed the initial debugging and performance verification of their OTDR system and
accelerated the launch of their products. Our solution provides critical technical support for the
development of OTDR systems in the demanding field of optical fiber control and can be further
extended to areas such as fiber optic communications network fault diagnosis and distributed fiber
optic sensing system development.

Case Study — Distributed Partial Discharge Monitoring Solution
With the rapid development of the new energy sector, the safety and stability of power systems
have become increasingly critical. Power monitoring systems are the core support technology for
grid operation and equipment management, ensuring safe, efficient and intelligent grid operation.
Regular monitoring of partial discharge signals in operational Gas-Insulated Switchgear (GIS) is an
effective means to ensure its safe operation. In the field of partial discharge, we collaborated with a
prominent high-tech enterprise, to build a distributed partial discharge monitoring system utilizing
our solution and peripherals.
Challenges:
. HighBandwidthandHighSamplingRateRequirements:Partialdischargesignalscanreach
frequencies exceeding 1 GHz, necessitating a sampling rate of over 2.5 GSa/s for
high-speed data acquisition and real-time storage.
. Multi-Channel Synchronization and Scalability: The number of monitoring sensors varies
with the scale of substations, requiring different numbers of acquisition channels. The
system must ensure easy expansion of channel numbers. To accurately locate discharge
points, all channels must be synchronized in data acquisition. In large-scale substations,
the distributed layout of monitoring equipment presents challenges in synchronizing
distributed devices.
. Real-TimeDataProcessingandAnalysis:Thesystemneedstoperformreal-timeintelligent
analysis and defect identification at the edge, reducing the load on backend servers.
Our Solutions and Advantages:
We offer customers comprehensive solutions with various forms of equipment to build
distributed monitoring systems. Our solution includes SUA8000 series products, which can support
up to 5GSa/s multi-channel synchronous sampling and offer various trigger modes to effectively
monitor different types of partial discharge signals. Our SUA8000 series, with each device able to
perform 8-channel signal acquisition, offering a single-channel sampling rate of 4GSa/s and a signal
bandwidth reaching up to 1.5GHz, effectively covering the ultra-high frequency monitoring signal
range. In conjunction with our synchronizers, we can achieve multi-device synchronous operations,
enabling the expansion of parallel monitoring channels. High stability time references and
multi-device synchronization mechanisms ensure temporal consistency across all acquisition
channels, effectively supporting time correlation and precise localization of partial discharge
signalsinlarge-scalesubstations.Additionally,ourcompactdesignallowseasydeploymentforsmall
to medium sites and can scale to hundreds of channels, integrating with various monitoring
applications. The device supports a wide range of software interfaces, with strong multi-system
compatibility, enabling user-driven customization and rapid integration into existing online
monitoring platforms.

By implementing this solution, our customer significantly enhanced the accuracy and efficiency
