Case Study — SPQ Platform Array Measurement and Control Solution
In the research field of optoelectronic control, traditional instruments fail to meet the rapidly
evolving customized demands due to their rigid functionalities and limited scalability. This is
particularly evident in their functional shortcomings in the unified scheduling of various terminals,
such as motion control, laser timing, and rotating mirror communications across various terminals.
LeveragingourSPQplatform,wedevelopedacoremeasurementandcontrolsystemwhichovercame
the limitations of traditional fixed instruments, for a research institute.
Our Solutions and Advantages:
We developed a core measurement and control system for high-performance photonic control
equipment based on the SPQ platform array measurement and control solution. This solution
utilizes ahigh-performance controller as the centralprocessingunit, and integrates variousmodules,
including AWG, high-precision digitizers, time measurement modules, and real-time computation
for precision control. It also integrated motion control, laser timing and rotating mirror
communications in the optoelectronic system, achieving picosecond level signal delay precision.
The measurement and control system can maintain timing jitter stability better than picoseconds
during 7/24 continuous operation. Additionally, it can provide real-time, low-latency feedback to
multiplesystems,suchaslasercontrolwaveformsandmotionplatforms,basedontheoptoelectronic
pulse measurement.
Value Propositions:
This case demonstrates our SPQ modular array measurement and control solution’s
unparalleled flexibility, exceptional synchronization precision, long-term operational reliability,
and future scalability. It has become the ideal platform for building complex, high-performance
centralized measurement and control applications, supporting engineers and scientists in
accelerating innovation in scientific research. Our SPQ platform array measurement and control
solution facilitates the rapid development of high-performance, customized test, measurement and
control systems, providing a solid foundation for intelligent innovation and development in the
education and research industry.
OUR CORE TECHNOLOGIES
With over two decades of dedicated R&D, we have established a vertically integrated
technology platform spanning hardware architecture, software architecture and algorithms, which
are critical components of our electronic test and measurement instruments and solutions. Based on
our deep technological accumulation and forward-looking R&D layout, this technology platform
enables us to address outstanding demands in high-growth markets such as communications, new
energy, semiconductors, and education and research.
Hardware Architecture
The traditional approach of instrument design, which involves developing each product from
the ground up, is relatively slow and inefficient. In contrast, our hardware strategy is a faster, and
adaptable approach built on three core pillars: our proprietary ASIC technology platforms,
standardized interfaces and a Common Building Blocks to enable agility and faster time to market.
Proprietary ASIC Technology Platforms as the Core
Recognizing that commercial off-the-shelf components can impose performance and
integration limitations, we have strategically focused on developing proprietary ASIC technology
platforms. This strategy allows us to establish a significant competitive advantage and forms the
foundation of our products’ core competency. We have successfully launched a series of ASIC
technology platforms, including:
. “Phoenix” Platform: this platform was launched in 2017, which achieved a maximum
bandwidth of 5GHz. According to Frost & Sullivan, we were the first PRC company to
have successfully commercialized digital oscilloscopes with self-developed ASICs.
– 121 –

=== PAGE 131 ===
BUSINESS
. “Centaurus” Platform: this platform was launched in 2022, which introduced a 12-bit
vertical resolution to our digital oscilloscopes, significantly enhancing the performance of
our entry-level and mid-range instruments.
. “Andromeda” Platform: this platform was launched in 2023, which featured in the first
high-performance digital oscilloscopes in China, achieving a maximum bandwidth of
13GHz.
Standardized Interfaces to Interconnect
At the interconnect of our hardware architecture is the proprietary RIGOL General Internal
Bus standard. This standard enables us to design critical hardware functions as independent,
reusable modules. This “decoupling” approach facilitates the rapid development of new instruments
by allowing the combination and configuration of existing modules, rather than initiating each
design from scratch. This has been applied across our entire product portfolio, significantly
enhancing our R&D efficiency, product quality, and ease of maintenance in the long term.
Common Building Blocks for Rapid Development
Our products comprised versatile modules that serve as Common Building Blocks. This
approach empowers us to construct custom, multi-functional test systems rapidly by integrating
various modules. This approach provides exceptional scalability and efficiency, allowing us to
quickly develop not only traditional benchtop instruments but also complex, industry-specific
solutions, particularly for automated test environments in the semiconductors and next-generation
communications industries.
Together, these three pillars form a cohesive and powerful hardware architecture. As a result,
we build the agility to efficiently develop products and customized solutions that meet evolving
market demands.
Software Architecture
Thedevelopmentofbespokesoftwareforeachnewinstrumenthasbeenasignificantbottleneck
within the industry, impeding innovation and increasing difficulties in maintenance. To address
thesechallenges,wehaveadoptedaunifiedandlayeredsoftwarearchitecturespecificallydesignedto
maximize reusability and accelerate the pace of development.
Our software architecture comprises several distinct and standardized layers. At its foundation
istheRIGOLOperatingSystem,acustomizedembeddedsystemthatprovidesaconsistenthardware
abstraction layer, which provides a standardized interface between the hardware of RIGOL
OperatingSystemandthehigher-levelsoftware.Thisfoundationallayerensuresthatourupper-level
software operates independently of specific underlying hardware. On top of this Operating System,
we have developed standardized middleware and a comprehensive set of drivers, enabling
collaboration between different functional modules and provide standardized remote-control
interfaces, for seamless automation. The architecture is completed by a unified application
framework with a common user interface library, ensuring a consistent user experience across all
products.
This structured, multi-layered approach forms the core of our software development strategy.
Byenablingourteamstofocusonapplication-levelinnovationratherthanrepeatedlyreconstructing
core infrastructure, it significantly accelerates the development and iteration of new instruments.
Supported by a robust software management system, it facilitates efficient collaboration among our
teams across different locations. This standardized structure not only streamlines product
development but also provides the flexibility to integrate our instruments into complex,
customized solutions, enhancing our ability to meet diverse market needs.

Algorithms
The raw data captured by an instrument’s hardware consists of numerical streams. The true
value of measurement is realized through algorithms that convert these data into precise, reliable,
and actionable insights. The algorithms serve as the intelligent “brain” of our technology system,
and our expertise in their development is a key differentiator for our Company. Our approach to
algorithm development focuses on three key areas:
. Hardware LevelAlgorithms:Prior to hardwarefabrication,weuse advanced algorithms to
virtuallydesignandtestourproducts.Throughsystem-levelsimulation,wecanaccurately
predict the performance of hardware and optimize designs and identify potential risks
earlyin thedevelopmentprocess,beforephysicalprototypesareproduced.Asaresult,we
are able to accelerate research and development cycles and improve the efficiency of
converting designs into high-quality products.
. Product Level Algorithms: Our algorithms are embedded within our instruments to ensure
superior accuracy and stability. For example, our automatic level control (“ALC”)
algorithm improves the stability of generated signals, while our adaptive signal denoising
technology effectively distinguishes genuine signals from background noise. In addition,
system-level calibration algorithms correct hardware imperfections, thereby maximizing
measurement accuracy. These embedded algorithms ensure that our instruments provide
faithful representation of real-world signals.
. Application Level Algorithms: At the application level, our advanced algorithms convert
high-fidelity data into meaningful insights for users, addressing specific challenges.
Building upon technologies such as vector modulation signal analysis for wireless
communications testing and automated compliance verification, we are increasingly
integrating AI-based algorithms tailored for practical applications, such as automatic
signal classification, detection of rare or abnormal events in large data streams, and
simplification of complex test procedures. These innovations transform our instruments
from conventional measurement tools to intelligent and problem-solving assistants that
deliver enhanced value to our customers.

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
Our industry features fast technological innovations with the emergence of next-generation
products every few years. We are committed to continuously advancing our technologies so as to
maintainourcompetitivenessandmarketshareandsustainoursuccess.Assuch,weplacesignificant
emphasis on strengthening our R&D capabilities. Our R&D expenses amounted to RMB142.9
million, RMB206.7 million and RMB225.9 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively, accounting
for 21.3%, 26.6% and 25.1%, respectively, of our revenue in the corresponding periods.
R&D Team
We have established a R&D network with four R&D centers in Suzhou, Beijing, Shanghai and
Xi’an in the PRC, and one R&D center in Malaysia. Our domestic R&D centers primarily focus on
R&D projects for advancing key technologies such as high-performance digital oscilloscopes,
high-frequency microwave and RF technology and wireless communication protocol analysis. Our
Malaysia R&D center primarily engages in research into the development of hardware modules,
solutions, and localized product improvements.
As of December 31, 2025, we maintained a R&D team of 327 personnel, with approximately
52.3% of our R&D personnel held a master’s or doctoral degree. Our core R&D personnel have an
average of more than 15 years of experience in the electronic test and measurement instrument and
solution industry.
Our R&D department primarily composed of the technology research team and the product
development team. We actively participate in domestic and overseas industry associations and
organizations,whichnotonlyincreaseourexposureandleadershipintheindustrybutalsoallowsus
to keep pace with the latest industry insights and market trends. We are a member of the LXI
Consortium, and serves as a committee member of the National Technical Committee on
Standardization of Electronic Measuring Instruments (全國電子測量儀器標準化技術委員會), and
have participated in the drafting and formulation of one national standard and three industry
general specifications. Additionally, we have established advanced R&D centers, including a
metrology laboratory that complies with the ISO/IEC 17025:2017 “General Requirements for the
Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories” and a CNAS laboratory accredited by the
China National Accreditation Service for Conformity Assessment.
Under the leadership of our founder and chairman, Dr. Wang Yue, we prioritize bridging lab
breakthroughs to mass production. Dr. Wang Yue is the pioneer of the domestic benchtop digital
oscilloscope industry and has over 27 years of expertise in the electronic test and measurement
industry. As the architect of our technology and product roadmap as well as core ASIC, he led the
development of our first virtual oscilloscope, paving the way for our entry into the electronic
measurement instrument market. His leadership ensures us to remain at the forefront of electronic
measurement technology innovation.
Product Design and Development
We have established detailed protocols and standard operating procedures for our product
design and development processes, which are essential for the success of our final products. Our
product design and development processes could vary due to different product specifications and
customer requirements. The average timeframe for most of our products is normally three to 36
months.

BUSINESS
To standardize the R&D process, we have formulated a comprehensive system for product
development. All R&D projects are required to undergo oversightand reviewat each stage. We have
set several technical review points for key technical nodes during the product development process.
Through early detection of product defects and risks in deliverables, problems and risks in stage
delivery can be identified as early as possible, and countermeasures and operational
recommendations can be formed to ensure that the entire product development process is
effectively controlled and managed.
The flowchart below summarizes the key steps of our product development process:
Concept Plan Develop Qualify Launch
High Level Development System
Provide Technical Design (HLD) & Unit Testing Integration Batch Validation Project Lessons
Alternative Plans Testing and Verification Learned and
and Select the Plan Support Team Building
Develop System Test Plan Structure Development Develop System Test Plan
. Concept Phase: The R&D process begins with product planning, where we identify
potential new products or technology upgrades based on market demand and emerging
technological trends. Our product development team validates the potential project from
various perspectives, such as market opportunities, market demand, costs, financial
feasibility, potential technical obstacles and risks, to determine whether the product
opportunity aligns with our overall strategic planning for products and technology.
. Planning Phase: If the concept passes the internal concept decision review, we proceed to
formalize the project initiation, including high level design and the development of a
system test plan. We initiate formal planning for development methods, including
comprehensive product definition, development and manufacturing methods, sales and
marketing plans, project management plans, product support plans, detailed schedules,
and financial analysis.
. Development Phase: After completing the conceptual design, the project enters the
development phase. This phase includes detailed product design, system integration and
test tape-out, manufacturing process design, manufacturing tool preparation,
manufacturing risk assessment, performance testing and product certification.
. Qualification Phase: In this phase, we perform rigorous design validation to ensure the
product meets all technical specifications and performance criteria. We will conduct mass
production tape-out, manufacturing system validation, optimization of production
processes and equipment, hardware/software stress testing and internal and external
customer beta testing.
. Launch Phase: As the final stage of product development, we focus on comprehensive
preparations for mass production release, ensuring that all systems and processes are
optimized for efficiency and scalability the finished goods meet our stringent performance
and safety standards. We conduct detailed profit and loss planning and drive the product
towards its official market launch, coordinating marketing and distribution efforts to
maximize impact and reach within the target market.

Distributor Sales
Given the diversity and large volume of our product offerings and end customers and the
significant variations in market conditions and customer preferences across different countries, we
strategicallycollaboratewithdistributorswhopossessextensivesaleschannelstoexpandourmarket
reach and effectively serve the needs of customers in various regions. According to Frost & Sullivan,
the use of a distribution model is in line with industry norms. Our distributors primarily include
leading global and regional distributors with comprehensive distribution networks, extensive
industry coverage, and robust supply chain management, as well as deep knowledge of relevant
jurisdictions or specific sectors.
Inourdistributorsalesmodel,wesellproductstothesedistributorsonabuyoutbasis,andthey
handle sales to end customers through their offline sales networks or e-commerce platforms. We
collaborate with our distributors to provide after-sales services and offer technical support to end
users as needed. We recognize revenue from distributor sales once products are delivered to the
distributors.
Our overall distributors are classified into contracted distributors and non-contracted
distributors. Contracted distributors typically enter into one year framework agreement with us,
whereasnon-contracteddistributorsprimarilytransactwithusonproject-by-projectbasistoaddress
specific tender qualification or supply qualification requirements of major customers. Contracted
distributorsaresubjecttoourpricingregimeandareentitledtoenhancedresourcessuchastechnical
support, product training, participation in marketing activities and rebate or promotional
arrangements. They are granted access to the ISM system to communicate and manage business
directly with us, and may, subject to an assessment of their contracted sales targets, business model
and customer profile, receive support in the form of credit terms. In contrast, pricing for
non-contracted distributors is determined on a project-by-project basis, and such distributors are
generally not eligible for credit terms or rebate arrangements. They are subject to independent
pricing determined for each project with regard to project size. We engage non-contracted
distributors as an efficient model to accommodate the specific requirements of our major customers,
while we also engage contracted distributors to maintain a stable, longer-term channel network. For
the avoidance of doubt, unless expressly specified as “non-contracted distributors,” references to
“distributors” herein refer to contracted distributors.
Inordertopromotethesalesofourproductsbyourdistributors,weprovidesalesrebatesfrom
time to time in order to incentivize our distributors. Our sales rebate is typically calculated as a
percentage of the overall sales value of the applicable products and is generally applied to
subsequent purchases by the respective distributors as credits instead of being provided in cash. The
actual sales rebate amounts vary greatly from time to time and are determined by a number of
factors, including market conditions, seasonality, competition, nature of the underlying products
and others.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our sales generated from distributor sales amounted to RMB485.9
million, RMB500.9 million and RMB586.0 million, respectively, accounting for 72.5%, 64.6% and
65.1% of our total revenues for these periods.

Relationship with Distributors
To the best of our knowledge, all of our distributors during the Track Record Period are
Independent Third Parties. To the best of our knowledge, there was no past or present relationship
(including business, employment, financing, family, trust or otherwise) between the distributors

our distributors and experienced no significant disputes or conflicts.
We carefully select our distributors by evaluating their capabilities in sales, solution
development, project implementation, after-sales service, and customization. When onboarding

BUSINESS
We manage our distributors in the following ways:
. Tiered Management: We have established a comprehensive distributor management
framework based on Integrated Sales Management system (“ISM system”), which
includes functional modules such as business opportunity management, sales
management, customer service and order management. The ISM system supports
multiple language versions, facilitating unified global sales management. We adopt a
tiered management system for our distributors based on their performance and respective
capabilities. Distributors who receive higher performance evaluations are eligible for
advantageous resource support, including technical assistance, training programs,
marketing activities and favorable credit terms. Our tiered management ensures that
our distributors have incentives to improve their performance and that resources are
allocated effectively. These efforts aim to strengthen our relationship with key
distributors and enable them to perform at their best.
. Anti-cannibalism and BusinessAllocation:We have also implemented a comprehensive and
structured system for opportunity allocation and approval to prevent market
cannibalization among our distributors. When potential business opportunities arise in
a specific market, distributors are required to report these opportunities through our ISM
system, ensuring visibility and proper tracking. Opportunities are allocated on a
“first-come, first-served” basis, meaning the distributor who first identifies and reports
the opportunity will be granted the lead. Additionally, we prioritize support for
distributors who have made substantial promotional efforts in the early stages. This
ensures that no distributors compete with another for the same end customer, thereby
maintaining a streamlined and efficient process. Additionally, this system ensures that
distributorship opportunities are allocated fairly.
. Distributor Enablement: To strengthen our distributors’ capabilities and improve their
service quality for end customers, we offer extensive training programs covering sales,
planning, and project implementation. Additionally, we carry out assessments of
distributors to further improve their capabilities, ensuring they are fully qualified to
represent our products and solutions effectively and deliver exceptional service.
We generally do not allow returns of products sold to distributors, except primarily for
defective products. According to Frost & Sullivan, our good return policy with distributors is in line
with the industry practice. Some of our distributors may use sub-distributors. They typically further
enter into agreements with the sub-distributors, and we generally do not enter into agreements or
directly establish relationships with the sub-distributors. Although we have no control over the
sub-distributors, we have implemented a digital tracking system, which tracks products throughout
the distribution chain via a unique code on the product’s packaging. Specifically, we match the
unique code on each product with the responsible distributor and the authorized sales region. When
end users activate a product, they are required to register the product’s unique code on our official
website or platform. Upon registration, our system automatically captures the actual geographic
location where the product is activated and used. If a product appears in an unauthorized region or
sales outlet, we can quickly identify the responsible distributor and prohibit the cross-regional
unauthorized sale. Furthermore, we monitor the sub-distribution channel through our regional
market oversight processes. Our ongoing communications with first-level distributors include
inquiries into the structure and performance of their downstream distribution networks.
Wepreventmarketcannibalizationthroughthefollowingmechanisms:(i)weclearlyspecifythe
distributor’s designated region in distribution agreement; (ii) distributors mainly focus on localized,
vertical e-commerce platforms in their respective regions, such as ZKH, a well-known electronic
product sales platform within the industry, as well as local online stores self-operated by our
overseas distributors, whereas our e-commerce sales prioritize well-known global e-commerce
platforms, such as Tmall and JD.com, to enhance brand visibility; and (iii) distributors may expand
their business beyond their authorized region by undergoing a rigorous “cross-regional project
registration and approval” process. Approval for cross-regional sales is granted only if a distributor
can demonstrate that it has invested more resources in the early stages and registered the project

BUSINESS
earlier than local regional distributors. Additionally, although both our Group and our distributors
have e-commerce sales, we have established a complementary relationship to prevent market
cannibalization. This is achieved through the following distinctions between our e-commerce sales
and those of our distributors: (i) our e-commerce sales encompass the entire product portfolio, with
an emphasis on newly launched products, whereas our distributors’ e-commerce channels are
dedicated to specific, high-demand mature models; and (ii) our e-commerce sales cater to customers
with relatively low purchase volumes and standardized needs, offering a streamlined and efficient
purchasing process. In contrast, our distributors’ e-commerce sales focus on high-value customers
with more complex technical requirements and application scenarios.
We believe that our products are at low risk of channel stuffing and cannibalization within our
distribution network due to: (i) we generally do not permit returns of products sold to distributors,
except for quality issues occurring during the warranty period, thereby eliminating incentives for
distributors to overstock; (ii) our distributors place orders with us based on market demand or
pre-agreed forecasts with their downstream clients, thereby minimizing speculative purchases; and
(iii) our distributors are typically engaged in or more familiar with specific product markets or
brands based on their expertise, industry experience and customer base, which reduces overlap and
direct competition among them.

ordered products if delivery to the distributors’ designated location is required.
Conversely, for distributors who choose to pick up products from our designated
location, they assume the costs and risks associated with the shipment of the ordered

customary industry practice.

RAW MATERIALS AND SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
The core raw material for our products include electronic raw materials, which primarily
consistofICchips,wafers,electroniccomponents,printedcircuitboards(“PCBs”)anddisplays.We
source raw materials domestically and from overseas countries. To minimize the risk of reliance on
any single supplier and maintain sourcing stability and bargaining power, we generally retain
multiple suppliers for our principal raw materials. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, the cost of raw materials
represented 72.3%, 67.8% and 72.5%, respectively, of our total cost of sales.
Our procurement process involves several key steps to ensure efficient supply management.
Initially, we engage in demand planning and supply strategy development, using rolling forecasts to
assess product demand and define strategies for managing supply volumes. This is followed by
procurement planning and ordering, where we create detailed plans and issue purchase orders to
suppliers. Suppliers then fulfill these orders, schedule shipments, and deliver the materials to
designated warehouses. Upon arrival, we inspect the raw materials and store them in stock
warehouses for production use.
– 138 –

=== PAGE 148 ===
BUSINESS
Our procurement strategy combines on-demand purchasing with strategic stockpiling. Using
historical data and demand forecasting, we maintain safety stock levels to ensure a stable supply
chain and uninterrupted production. In addition, we monitor market trends, price fluctuations of
raw materials, inventory, customer orders and capital allocation to make informed decisions about
stockpiling. This approach minimizes the risks of price volatility and ensures we stay agile in a
competitive and rapidly changing market. Based on demand forecasts, supplier pricing trends and
capacity planning, we create rolling procurement plans. These plans guide our purchasing team in
requesting quotes, placing orders and coordinating material deliveries. By maintaining close
relationships with qualified suppliers and ensuring clear communication, we are able to achieve
efficient procurement cycles while maintaining flexibility in responding to changes in market
demand.
We have implemented a rigorous supplier qualification and dynamic management system,
namely SRM system, to monitor the supplier admission, qualification audits, and performance
evaluations. We evaluate suppliers on multiple dimensions such as technical capability, quality,
delivery performance, service levels and cost-effectiveness. We uphold stringent requirements for
supplier admission, assessment, and auditing throughout the supplier lifecycle. Our supplier
assessment process evaluates quality, supply reliability, cost, technology and service indicators. We
also employ a tiered management strategy, incorporating rewards for excellence, supervised
improvement plans, and the removal of underperforming suppliers, thereby optimizing our supplier
base and maintaining our competitiveness.

. Quality control and Product Returns: All raw materials must comply with applicable
national and industry standards as well as our technical specifications. We conduct
inspections upon delivery and reserve the right to reject or return non-compliant goods.
Suppliers are responsible for resolving quality issues and shall replace defective goods.
They are also required to cover the logistics costs and assume the risks associated with
returning the defective products.
. Product Warranty: Generally one year after acceptance. During the warranty period,
suppliers shall repair defective products free of charge.
. Intellectual Property: Suppliers shall ensure that their products do not infringe upon any
third-party intellectual property rights, and they shall bear all legal responsibilities and
costs incurred by such kind of dispute.
. Termination: Generally, the contract can be terminated upon mutual agreement.
PRODUCTION
We have developed a manufacturing framework that strategically integrates global and
domestic resources primarily through in-house production. We primarily utilize our in-house
facilities to handle key production processes, including testing for self-developed ASICs,
surface-mount technology (“SMT”) production, product assembly, software programming,
functional testing, and quality inspection. These help ensure both quality and security, with
carefully crafted workflows to meet specific needs of major customers.

BUSINESS
Our manufacturing model is designed to accommodate the diverse requirements of our product
portfolio.Dependingontheproducttype,ourproductionprocessesincorporatearangeofadvanced
workflows, including:
. Planning and Procurement: our planning and procurement process involves several key
steps to ensure efficient supply management. Initially, we use rolling forecasts to assess
product demand and define strategies for managing supply volumes. This is followed by
procurement planning and ordering, where we create detailed plans and issue purchase
orders to suppliers. Suppliers then fulfill these orders, schedule shipments, and deliver the
materials to designated warehouses. Upon arrival, we inspect raw materials to verify their
quality and compliance with specifications and store them in warehouses for production
use.
. Production Preparation: production preparation encompasses production scheduling and
material kitting/allocation, which involve the determination of product types, production
quantities and timing, based on market demand and resource availability. It ensures
efficient use of resources and alignment with business goals. Once the plan is set,
production scheduling organizes tasks and assigns resources to specific periods,
optimizing workflow and ensuring timely completion of production orders, while
material kitting/allocation ensures that all necessary materials are available and
properly distributed for production.
. Manufacturing and Testing: including SMT production, where packaged electronic
components are precisely mounted onto products to ensure secure attachment, manual
insertion production, printed circuit board assembly (“PCBA”) testing and
electromechanical device assembly, testing and packaging, to ensure the quality and
reliability of the finished product before market release; and
. Quality Control and Delivery: Quality control is a critical component of our production
process, encompassing initial inspections during production, regular and outgoing quality
control (“OQC”) inspections, and independent quality engineers conducting
comprehensive tests on finished products. All products must pass 100% inspection
before being stored, ensuring they meet our stringent quality standards. This ensures that
high-quality products are delivered to our customers, maintaining the integrity and
reliability of our offerings throughout the storage and delivery process.
As we have developed our own production capacity, including the establishment of our
self-builtfactoriesinSuzhou and Penang,alongwiththecompletionofcustomerintegration and the
ramp-up of production lines into full operation, our manufacturing ability has been steadily
increased.
In addition to our in-house production, we outsource certain manufacturing processes,
primarily involving PCBA processing for products such as power supplies, digital oscilloscopes,
waveform generators, multimeters and probes. We typically engage third-party manufacturers in
circumstances where the components or products have relatively low technological requirements for
their production. This strategy allows us to free up our SMT production capacity, ensuring the
quality and timely delivery of our mid-range and high-performance products.

QUALITY MANAGEMENT
We have established a comprehensive set of quality control and assurance procedures to
monitor our operations to ensure compliance with the regulatory requirements and quality
requirements during the entire development, manufacturing, delivery and services processes. We
have established a quality traceability system to achieve full traceability from raw materials to
finishedproducts,anddynamicallymonitorkeyqualityparameters.Duringproduction,weuseMES
for real-time monitoring and combine it with automated testing to ensure consistency. From
incoming material inspection to final outgoing inspection, we conduct comprehensive testing of
product functions, performance and reliability to ensure that the delivered products meet industry
standards. We have obtained the ISO 9001:2015, ISO/IEC 17025:2017, CE certification and
cTUVus/UL certification. We have also been officially authorized by the LXI Consortium as a
testing and certification center, becoming the only LXI-authorized testing and certification unit in
the Asia-Pacific region.
We strictly implement rigorous quality control measures and establish a comprehensive
customer feedback and complaint handling process to promptly and effectively address customer
concerns. We have mainly implemented the following procedures for quality control:
. Raw Material Inspection and Selection: We have established a strict certification process
for selecting qualified suppliers and a comprehensive evaluation and introduction process
for new raw materials, along with rigorous material inspection standards.
. Production Process Monitoring: We have set up key quality control points throughout the
production process to enable on-site inspections and monitoring so that we could identify
potential issues promptly. Critical parameters and data are recorded in real-time for
subsequent analysis and traceability.
. Product Inspection and Testing: We have implemented a comprehensive product quality
inspection standard, along with non-conforming product and abnormality management
standards.Everyproductundergoes100%inspectiontoguaranteethequalityofoutgoing
shipments.
. Employee Skill Training: All of our employees undergo rigorous training and pass
competency assessments. Additionally, we regularly organize professional skills and
quality awareness training to continuously improve employees’ quality consciousness and
technical proficiency.
. Quality Records and Management: We maintain a robust quality record system to ensure
data integrity and traceability. We conduct statistical analysis of quality data to identify
potential issues for improvement timely, fostering continuous enhancement of product
quality.

The salient terms of our agreements with third-party logistics service providers are set forth
below:
. Shipment and delivery: Logistics service providers are responsible for the delivery of the
products to the locations designated by us within the agreed time frame.
. Pricing: The delivery service fee varies based on distance and item’s category, size and
weight. The delivery service fee is settled on a monthly basis.
. Credit Term: Logistics service providers typically grant us a credit term of 25 days.
. Insurance and Compensation: Logistics service providers are responsible for compensation
for any damage or loss of the products occurring during transportation. They may also
offer insurance coverage for the products on an opt-in basis at rates and terms
communicated in advance.
. Duration: The agreements are typically effective for one year.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not (i)

delivery or mishandling of products by our logistics service providers, or (iii) have any disputes with
our logistics service providers.

DATA PRIVACY AND SECURITY
We do not have access to or control over the data stored in our products once they are sold to
customers. In the course of conducting our business, we primarily collect the following types of user
data: contact information, delivery addresses and purchase records. We collect their payment
information as part of purchase records to complete the transactions when customers make
purchases. In addition, we also collect the basic information of our distributors and their designated
contacts to facilitate management. Adhering to the principle of data minimization, we collect only
the essential personal information from our customers, distributors, suppliers and other third-party
service providers solely to facilitate the sales and delivery of our products, as well as to provide
after-sales services and conduct marketing activities and we have obtained consent for the collection
of such personal data.
We have established a comprehensive data security and information management system to
ensure the integrity of our systems and the privacy of our data. We have implemented several
security measures, including firewalls, intrusion prevention systems, regular penetration tests,
vulnerability scans, and disaster recovery plans. We also encrypt data and utilize email security
protection systems. We have also adopted rigorous encrypted algorithm to store sensitive data and
strictlyexecuteadataaccessingand transmittingpolicytoensuretheconfidentialityofourdata.We
have developed strict internal control and data accessing mechanisms and detailed approval and
operation procedures regarding data storage and processing, and established a set of internal
protocols on data security, which set forth detailed, stringent requirements in relation to the use,
disclosureandprotectionofconfidentialinformation.Wehaveestablishedandimplementedinternal
standards which require a thorough legality and security assessment of any third-party data
processing activities before commencing cooperations. In accordance with these standards, we
conduct formal onboarding reviews of the third-party service providers to verify the lawfulness of
their processing, evaluate their technical and organizational safeguards and ensure an appropriate
level of data protection. Additionally, we generally enter into data processing agreements or
incorporate data processing clauses in the contracts with third-party service providers, which clearly
set out each party’s data protection obligations and responsibilities, including restrictions on use,
confidentiality, security controls and incident notification. These internal measures collectively help
to ensure that third-party service providers safeguard customers’ sensitive data and process it in a
lawful, secure and accountable manner. We conduct regular maintenance, inspections and technical
upgrades on computers, servers, and IT infrastructure. We have a comprehensive data backup
system to encrypt and store data on servers in different locations in order to minimize the risk of
data loss. The data generated from domestic operations is stored on domestic servers, while data
from international operations is stored on servers located abroad. We generally do not engage in
cross-border data transmission. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable

transmissions do not involve any sensitive personal information and do not include any important

disclosures.

ESG Risk Management
We have adopted the following measures to identify, assess, manage and mitigate ESG risks.
Risks Related to the Environment and Climate
We recognize the potential financial and reputational risks related to the environment,
including those stemming from adherence to prevailing environmental regulations and stringent
standards. For example, China’s carbon neutrality objective established in 2020, which aims to have
CO2 emissions peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060, may lead to increased
costs related to energy procurement, as we may be required to incur transition costs in procuring
green energy that can be more expensive than energy generated from conventional sources, or bear
the costs of purchasing or upgrading our equipment.
We continue to improve our management system for environmental sustainability and promote
effective implementation of environmental protection measures. We have established the HSE
(Health, Safety, and Environment) Management Committee to conduct a comprehensive
environment management, as well as the Energy Conservation and Emission Reduction Work
Panel focused on green production. In addition, we have issued and implemented measures for
identifying, evaluating, monitoring and mitigating environmental factors and for waste
management, as well as other related protocols to enhance our environmental protection effort at
an institutional level. We actively encourage our employees and business partners to participate in
environmental initiatives and attend trainings and educational sessions.

Measures on Managing Environmental Risks
We seek to minimize the impact on the environment and enhance environmental sustainability

green production. In addition, we have developed a series of internal guidelines and procedures for

We actively respond to the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals by continuously
optimizing our energy usage structure and reducing our carbon emissions. We have adopted various
energy-saving measures and we’re focusing on incorporating green and low-carbon practices from
the onset of our operations. We have obtained ISO 14001 certification, which is a testament to our
environment management capability and product carbon footprint. In addition, we have
implemented a series of measures in our daily operations to mitigate environmental risks:
. Emergency Management of Environmental Risks: We have established a comprehensive
emergency mechanism for sudden environmental incidents. We adhere to the principle of
classified management, addressing pollution characteristics from different sources. We
leverage departmental expertise to implement precise and effective preventive measures,
aiming to minimize or reduce the occurrence of sudden environmental incidents and
eliminate or mitigate the long-term impacts caused by such incidents.
. Conducting Environmental Safety Inspections: We continuously advance various safety
inspection efforts to ensure the normalization of safe production. With a comprehensive
safety supervision and management process, we effectively implement the environmental
safety management system, achieving significant results in preventing and reducing
accidents, thereby ensuring safe production and environmental safety.

. Energy Management: To continuously improve energy utilization efficiency and
environmental performance, we have established a Energy Conservation and Emission
Reduction Work Panel. By using smart energy management systems and smart logistics
systems, we significantly reduced overall energy consumption, promoting efficient
resource utilization and providing new solutions to green manufacturing and

. Water Resource Management: We actively introduce water-saving technologies and
equipment, optimize production processes, and effectively reduce water resource
consumption. Additionally, we regularly inspect water facilities, strengthen daily
maintenance management, and eliminate water resource waste. Furthermore, we
continuously enhance employees’ awareness and habits of saving water, contributing to
the protection of water resources.
. Packaging Material Management: We optimize and recycle product packaging,
prioritizing the use of recyclable, degradable, or low environmental impact materials.
We continuously explore opportunities to reduce the use of packaging materials and

product lifecycle.
. Gas Pollutants Discharge: We actively explore and practice effective gas pollution
treatment solutions, committed to creating a green and sustainable operational model.
For example, we have introduced three sets of exhaust gas treatment facilities:
“high-temperature incinerator + scrubbing + secondary activated carbon adsorption”,
“alkalinescrubbingtower”,and“secondaryactivated carbon adsorption”.These facilities
have significantly improved the efficiency of exhaust gas purification, ensuring that the
emissions of various gas pollutants meet the relevant standards.
. Wastewater Discharge: We strictly adhere to relevant regulations for effective wastewater
management. Our wastewater mainly includes pure water concentrate and employee
domesticsewage,whichisconnectedtothelocalwaterqualitypurification plantsthrough
the municipal sewage network for centralized treatment. We continue to decrease the
generation of industrial wastewater emissions, which reflects our responsibility for
environmental protection.
. Solid Waste Management: We have established a comprehensive solid waste management
system. For non-hazardous waste, the general industrial solid waste is collected by the
relevant department for comprehensive utilization and treatment; and domestic waste is
collected and processed by local sanitation departments. Hazardous waste is temporarily
stored and entrusted to qualified third-party companies for treatment. We have also
established an internal emergency team to effectively prevent and handle hazardous waste
spill incidents and secondary risks triggered. Additionally, We organizes various forms of
hazardous waste pollution prevention education and protection business training,
continuously enhancing employees’ hazardous waste management and disposal
capabilities.
. Green Product Design: We closely follow the industry development trend of promoting
green, efficient, and energy-saving products under the “dual carbon” goals, integrating
green environmental protection concepts into product design. We examine environmental
impactsfromtheproductlifecycle,simplifyproductcomponents,userecyclablematerials,
improve resource utilization, and advance product greening.

During the Track Record Period, we were involved in the following legal proceedings.
LegalProceedings with Suzhou Shundi Construction Engineering Co., Ltd Regarding Contract Dispute
In June 2022, we entered into an equipment maintenance and repair contract with Suzhou
Shundi Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (“Shundi”). Pursuant to the contract, Shundi was
required to provide equipment maintenance and repair services as well as on-site personnel services
to us. During the course of Shundi’s performance of the contract, however, we discovered that
Shundi had committed multiple breaches, including deploying non-employees to perform services,
lacking proper qualifications and professional competence, and acting in bad faith by concealing the
availability of free manufacturer repairs and attempting to misappropriate spare parts. Accordingly,
we issued a notice of termination of the contract in October 2024.
On December 31, 2024, Shundi filed a lawsuit against us, alleging that we had failed to pay
outstanding service fees following the termination of the contract. Shundi sought RMB350,000 in
outstanding service fees with accrued interest, RMB534,000 as a contractual penalty, and
reimbursement of legal and preservation costs. On the basis of Shundi’s breaches during the
performance of the contract, we filed a counterclaim seeking a full refund of RMB1,716,019.96,
being the total amounts paid to Shundi under the contract.

under which we agreed to make a one-time payment of RMB340,000 to Shundi by January 15, 2026.

had strong factual grounds supporting our counterclaim, the court may apply equitable principles
and decline to order a full refund of service fees even where the services rendered were deficient. The

The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (“the OECD”), an
international organization of cross-border cooperation, promulgated the transfer pricing
guidelines for multinational enterprises and tax administration (“the OECD TP Guidelines”),
which are generally followed by, or are consistent with, the tax laws and regulation in the relevant
tax jurisdictions involved in the related party transaction, including PRC, Hong Kong SAR, United
States, Germany and Malaysia. According to the OECD TP Guidelines, intra-group transactions
should be conducted on an arm’s length basis to avoid distorted taxable income in different
jurisdictions.
We have engaged independent third party transfer pricing tax adviser, Shanghai Deloitte Tax
Ltd. Suzhou Branch (“Transfer Pricing Tax Advisor”), to conduct benchmarking studies and to
review whether our intra-Group transactions in relation to the provision of software products,
semi/finished products, and various service are compliant with the arm’s length principle in
accordance with the OECD TP Guidelines.
Transfer Pricing Methodologies and the Basis of the Conclusion
Based on the functional and risk analysis performed by our Transfer Pricing Tax Advisor, the
Tested Transactions are centered on the Company’s production and manufacturing operations and
comprise a continuous chain of activities, including external procurement of raw materials,
procurement of supporting software from related parties followed by integrated manufacturing, and
sales to external customers and Group entities for its further resale in different jurisdictions. Based
on the function and risk profiles of the entities within the Group and characteristics of the Tested
Transactions, the Transactional Net Margin Method (“TNMM”) is selected as the appropriate
transfer pricing method to evaluate the above-mentioned intra-Group transactions during the Track
Record Period. The TNMM is usually applied to related party transactions involving purchases,
sales, transfer and use of tangible assets, transfer and use of intangible assets, and provision of
services, etc. This method analyzes the profit level indicators and is less affected by transactional
differences or accounting practice discrepancies.
According to the functional and risk analysis performed by our Transfer Pricing Tax Advisor,
the Company is a manufacturer with certain intangible assets, RIGOL Malaysia is the routine
manufacturer and our overseas subsidiaries RIGOL HK, RIGOL EU and RIGOL USA are routine
distributers within the Group. Accordingly, the Company, RIGOL HK, RIGOL USA, RIGOL EU,
and RIGOL Malaysia were selected as the tested parties within our Group, of which their financial
data are readily available, and their profits can be measured reliably, consistent with the selection
principles for tested parties under the TNMM.
– 164 –

=== PAGE 174 ===
BUSINESS
Under the TNMM, our Transfer Pricing Tax Advisor selected groups of independent
comparable manufacturers to the Company and RIGOL Malaysia, and comparable distributors
to RIGOL HK, RIGOL USA and RIGOL EU to ascertain the arm’s length returns for the tested
parties.To identifycomparablecompanies,ORBIS databasepublishedbyBureau VanDijk (“BvD”)
is used. The search process is to first identify the pool of potential active comparable companies
based on relevant Standard Industrial Code, independence indicator and geographical location.
Secondly, quantitative criteria are applied to eliminate companies that have insufficient financial
data or report consecutive losses during the Track Record Period. Thirdly, qualitative screening is
performedonthebusinessdescriptions,financialdatafromthedatabaseandinformationfromother
sources (e.g., Company websites, annual reports) to eliminate companies with functions or
products/services significantly different from the tested parties’ functions and business. After
applying the above searching and screening criteria, independent companies that are comparable in
terms of functions performed and risks assumed by the tested parities are identified. Their available
financial results relevant to the Track Record Period are summarized to calculate the inter-quartile
range as the arm’s length returns.
Profit level indicators (“PLIs”) are ratios that measure relationships between profits and sales
generated, costs incurred, or resources employed. The appropriateness of a given PLI in a particular
TNMManalysisdependsonthenatureoftheactivitiesofthetestedpartyaswellasonthereliability
of the available data. After reviewing the PLIs, the Full Cost Mark Up (“FCMU”) ratio was chosen
as the most reliable PLI to evaluate the arm’s length nature of the results achieved by the Company
with respect to the related party transactions under evaluation. Return on Sales (“ROS”) ratio was
chosen as the most reliable PLI to evaluate the arm’s length nature of the results achieved by
distributor with respect to the related party transactions under evaluation. Details of financial
results for each tested party are set out as below:

THIRD PARTY PAYMENT
Background and Reasons
During the Track Record Period, we accepted payments made on behalf of certain customers
(the “Relevant Customer(s)”), through the accounts of third-party payors who were not affiliated
companies of the Relevant Customers but were designated by the Relevant Customers (the
“Third-PartyPaymentArrangement(s)”).Thethird-partypayorsareindependentthird-partytrading
companies of the Relevant Customer(s) designated by the Relevant Customers. According to Frost
&Sullivan, itisa commoncommercial practice for customersto settle paymentsthrough third-party
payors for various personal reasons. The main reason for the Third-Party Payment Arrangements in
our business is that overseas customers often opt for third-party payment methods for their
convenience and flexibility.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, there were nine, seven and four Relevant Customers, respectively, and
the aggregate amount of Third Party Payment Arrangement was RMB6.2 million, RMB5.5 million
and RMB2.0 million, representing approximately 0.9%, 0.7% and 0.2% of our total revenues,
respectively. No individual Relevant Customer had made material contribution to our revenue
during the Track Record Period. To the best of our knowledge, none of the Third-Party Payors
designatedbytheRelevantCustomerisourconnectedperson,andalldesignatedThird-PartyPayors
are independent from each of our Directors, senior management and Controlling Shareholders.
Implication of the Third-Party Payment Arrangements
During the Track Record Period, our Directors confirm that: (i) we had not provided any
discount, commission, rebate, or other benefit to any of the Relevant Customers to facilitate or
incentivize the Third-Party Payment Arrangements, (ii) the pricing and payment terms of the
agreements we entered into with the Relevant Customers were generally in line with customers not
– 166 –

BUSINESS
involved in the Third-Party Payment Arrangements under similar scenarios and (iii) the Third-Party
Payment Arrangements have been recorded completely and accurately in our accounting books and
records in all material respects.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, as confirmed by the
Directors, (i) all settlements were based on bona fide underlying transactions and valid contractual
relationships, (ii) the settlement amounts were consistent with the amounts incurred under the
relevant transactions, (iii) we were not aware of any instances of commercial bribery, money

Internal Control Measures for Third-Party Payment Arrangement
To safeguard our Company’s interest against risks associated with Third-Party Payment
Arrangements, the following internal control measures have been adopted by our Company
(collectively, the “Rectification Measures”):
. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we had ceased all Third-Party Payment Arrangements
and required our customers to settle the payments directly with us.
. Wecirculatednoticeinternallytoalertandinformrelevantstaffmembersofrequirements
on identification of, and prohibition on accepting Third-Party Payment Arrangement;
. Our finance department is responsible for maintaining a receipt settlement management
ledger, which records, among other information, the customer’s name, content of
transaction, payment data, payment sum, payment method and the payer’s name, so as to
ensure that relevant payments are made directly by the relevant customer;
. We require our customers to make payments using their own legitimate bank accounts.
Payments from third-party accounts that do not match the contracting party are strictly
prohibited. In case of any such discrepancy, the received payment will be returned, and
the contractual counterparty will be required to make the payment again through their
own account;
. To prevent fraud or money laundering activities and ensure the accuracy and
completeness of our accounting books and records, we consistently maintained our
know-your-customer procedures to gain a comprehensive understanding of our customers
and performed verification of payment details against our records to confirm payments
are made in accordance with the agreements and/or the undertaking letters. If any
abnormalities are detected, we will promptly liaise with such customers for verification
and correction.

IMPACT OF U.S. TARIFFS
All items exported to the U.S. are subject to U.S. Tariffs. Since February 2025, the U.S.
proposed to impose multiple rounds of tariffs on a wide range of goods imported from multiple
countries, including China, and China responded with retaliatory tariffs. Since February 2025, both
countries raised reciprocal tariffs on each other’s imported goods to 125%. However, on May 12,
2025, both the U.S. and China modified these tariff measures: the U.S. removed the 125% tariff and
temporarily reduced tariffs on Chinese goods to 10% by suspending a 24% duty for 90 days. The
PRC government announced the same tariff adjustments, removing the 125% retaliatory tariff and
cutting tariffs on U.S. goods from 34% to 10% for the same period. This suspension was further
extended by the two countries for an additional 90 days until November 10, 2025. Following the two
countries’ trade negotiations on October 30, 2025, on November 1, 2025, the U.S. announced that it
agreed to suspend for one year a 24% reciprocal tariff on Chinese products and reduce the
fentanyl-related tariff on Chinese products by 10%. In addition, China agreed to adjust its counter
measures related to the above U.S. tariffs, and the two countries agreed to continue extending
certain tariff exemptions. On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court held that the International
Emergency Economic Power Act (the “IEEPA”) does not authorize the President to impose tariffs,
including the reciprocal and fentanyl-related tariffs. Effective from February 24, 2026, the U.S.
customs authority will cease to collect these tariffs. Meanwhile, President Trump issued a
proclamation to impose a temporary import surcharge of 10% on all imports to the U.S. effective
from February 24, 2026 for a period of 150 days, and later announced this tariff rate would be 15%
(the rateoftheactualimport surcharge may vary,subjectto themodification oftherelevantrules to
effectuate the collection of such surcharge). As advised by our International Sanctions Legal
Advisor, there are various types of tariffs imposed by the U.S., including tariff regimes of the U.S.
set forth in the Section 301 (the “Section 301 Tariffs”) and Section 122 (“Section 122 Tariffs”) of the
Trade Act of 1974, the Most-Favored-Nation tariffs (the “MFN Tariffs”), the reciprocal tariffs
(“IEEPA Reciprocal Tariffs”) and the fentanyl tariff (“IEEPA Fentanyl Tariffs”) under IEEPA
– 169 –

BUSINESS
(together, the IEEPA Tariffs”) (collectively, the “U.S. Tariffs”). Among the aforementioned tariffs,
the Section 301 Tariffs are product-specific and apply to products of China (including Hong Kong
and Macau) only. Our products are subject to 7.5%, 15% or 25% Section 301 Tariffs, depending on
the type of the products (and accessories), during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest

the U.S. manufactured from our production facilities in Penang are predominately subject only to
product-specific MFN Tariffs and country-specific Section 122 Tariffs, as of the Latest Practicable
Date, and paid by our U.S. subsidiary as the importer on record. Since our Malaysian-origin
products are not subject to the Section 301 Tariffs targeting Chinese-origin products, the total
amount of tariffs incurred on our sales to the U.S. has declined over the Track Record Period as the
proportion of products supplied by our production facilities in Penang has continued to grow.

RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL
It is the responsibility of our Board to ensure that we maintain sound and effective internal
controls and risk management system to safeguard our shareholders’ investment and our assets. We
maintaininternalmanualswhichsetoutoperatingprocedures,internalcontrolproceduresandother
policies and guidelines. We have adopted and implemented comprehensive risk management policies
in various aspects of our business operations, including financial reporting, IT, compliance,
intellectual property, human resources, and investment management.
Our Board of Directors are responsible for the establishment, updating and implementation of
our internal control policies and systems, while our management team monitors the daily
implementation of the internal control procedures and measures with respect to our functional
teams. Our Directors are of the view that our current internal control measures are adequate and
effective to ensure compliance with relevant laws and regulations.
Operational Risk Management
Operational risk refers to the risk of direct or indirect financial loss resulting from incomplete
orproblematicinternalprocesses,personnelmistakes,ITsystemfailuresorexternalevents.Wehave
established a series of internal procedures to manage such risks. We take a comprehensive approach
with regard to operational risk management, and we have implemented a mechanism with detailed
and decentralized responsibilities and clear rewards and punishment systems. Our IT, human
resources, finance and operations departments are collectively responsible to ensure the compliance
of our operations with internal procedures. In the event of a major adverse event, the matter will be
escalated to our legal department to take appropriate measures. Through effective operational risk
management, we expect to control operational risks within a reasonable range by identifying,
measuring, monitoring and containing operational risks to reduce potential losses.
Human Resources Risk Management
We provide regular and specialized training tailored to the needs of our employees in different
departments. These trainings enable our staff to improve their skills and better address our
customers’ needs. We have in place an employee handbook approved by our management and
distributed to all our employees, which contains internal rules and guidelines regarding best
commercial practices, work ethics, fraud prevention mechanisms, negligence, and corruption.

=== PAGE 181 ===
BUSINESS
Financial Reporting and Risk Management
We have in place a set of accounting policies in connection with our financial reporting risk
management, such as financial report management policies, treasury management policies, and
reimbursement management policies. We have various procedures in place to implement accounting
policies, and our financial department reviews our management accounts based on such procedures.
Credit Risk Management
We seek to maintain strict control over our outstanding receivables and have implemented a
policy to minimize credit risk. We maintain regular communication with our customers, address
potentialpayment issuesproactively, andconductdetailed risk assessments. Our finance department
conducts regular reviews of overdue accounts and recoverability of our outstanding balances,
prioritizing high-value or long-overdue balances, and when appropriate, provides for impairment of
these trade receivables. Our sales department is responsible for collecting outstanding receivables,
particularly following up on any overdue accounts. For significantly overdue accounts with no
resolution, we escalate to legal proceedings.
Audit Committee Experience and Qualification and Board Oversight
To monitor the ongoing implementation of our risk management policies, we have established
an Audit Committee to review and supervise our financial reporting process and internal control
system on an ongoing basis to ensure that our internal control system is effective in identifying,
managing and mitigating risks involved in our business operations. See “Directors and Senior
Management — Management and Corporate Governance — Board Committees — Audit
Committee.” We have also established an internal audit department which is responsible for
reviewing the effectiveness of internal controls and reporting issues identified and improving our
internal control system and procedures by identifying internal control failures and weaknesses on an
ongoing basis. The internal audit department reports any major issues identified to the Audit
Committee and Board of Directors on a timely basis.

OVERVIEW
We are an electronic test and measurement instrument company in the PRC with advanced
technology capabilities and extensive global footprint. According to Frost & Sullivan, we are the
largest PRC electronic test and measurement instrument provider and ranked eighth globally in
terms of revenue in 2025. We design, develop, manufacture and deliver a comprehensive suite of
electronic test and measurement instruments and solutions that power scientific discovery and
industrial innovation. Under the “RIGOL” brand, we serve a diverse customer base of over 100,000
end customers across more than 90 countries and regions, addressing complex test challenges across
communications, new energy, semiconductors, and education and research sectors. We are
committed to innovation and in-house mastery of core technologies. Through sustained advances
in hardware, software and algorithms, we have built a proprietary core technology platform and
established ourselves as a competitive electronic test and measurement enterprise.
Through years of dedicated research and development and innovation, we have established a
comprehensive electronic test and measurement offering built on two pillars: (i) a
core-technology-driven product matrix, encompassing digital oscilloscopes, microwave and RF
instruments, DC and precision instruments, and modular instruments, and (ii) a suite of
multi-scenario solutions, primarily serving high-growth industries including communications, new
energy, semiconductors, and education and research.

MAJOR FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our results of operations and financial performance are influenced by a variety of
industry-wide and business-specific drivers. The following discussion sets out the principal factors
that management believes are most significant to our results of operations, drawing on industry
trends, our product and technology strategy and operational execution during the Track Record
Period and beyond.
Market Growth of the Global Electronic Test and Measurement Instrument and Solution Industry and
Our Ability to Compete in the Global Market
Our financial performance is significantly influenced by the growth of the global electronic test
and measurement instrument and solution industry, which can be affected by the downstream
market size and customer demand, and our ability to compete effectively in this market. According
to Frost & Sullivan, the global market size of electronic test and measurement instruments and
solutionsin2025achievedoverRMB110billion.Lookingahead,themarketisprojectedtomaintain
strong growth momentum, with an estimated CAGR of 9.6% from 2026 to 2030, reaching
approximately RMB180 billion in 2030.
Demand for our products is closely tied to the industry’s growth trajectory. The global
electronic test and measurement industry is driven by new technological advancements which will
bring product iteration, and growth in the downstream markets. At the same time, the industry is
experiencing trends such as higher performance and enhanced tool efficiency and a shift toward
more intelligent and integrated solutions. We believe our full-stack, proprietary technological
capabilities, diverse range of electronic test and measurement instruments and ability to deliver
integrated solutions addressing specific industry challenges, will provide us with better competitive
edge to meet the increasing demands of downstream markets.
In the electronic test and measurement instrument and solution market, we compete with
multinational incumbents and emerging domestic brands on technological advancement, product
performance and pricing flexibility. We have maintained a competitive edge and will continue to
focus on advancing technological strength, understanding of customer needs and steady
improvement of profitability. To sustain high gross profit margin and defend market share, we
will continue to strengthen our ability to differentiate through proprietary ASIC technology
platforms, advanced signal processing algorithms, our comprehensive application software
ecosystem and our solutions.
Our Ability to Continue Innovation and Technological Advancements
Our long-term market position is built on our sustained leadership in product innovation and
technological advancements. The process for technology development and product design involves
long investment cycles. As the first and only PRC company to have successfully commercialized
digital oscilloscopes with self-developed ASICs, our ongoing commitment to technology
development has already resulted in differentiated products and solutions, reinforcing our
technological leadership in the market. We believe our ability to execute R&D initiatives, develop
new technologies, launch new products and enhance existing products, alongside our success in
attracting and retaining top R&D talent, is essential in maintaining our market position.
We have invested,and plan to continue to invest, significant resources in our R&Defforts. Our
R&D expenses accounted for 21.3%, 26.6% and 25.1% of our total revenue in 2023, 2024 and 2025,
respectively. Specifically, the progress of our technology and product development depends largely
on our R&D talents. As of December 31, 2025, our R&D team consisted of 327 members,
representing 46.8% of total employees as of the same date. These investments support ongoing
projects such as our high-performance and high-resolution oscilloscope platform, next-generation
RF signal chain, and integrated application software. In order to continue to scale and expand our
operations, we will continue to enhance our R&D efficiency and prioritize high-impact projects to
accelerate time-to-market for new products and solutions, and successfully commercialize R&D
outcomes.

Our Ability to Develop and Enhance Our Portfolio of Products and Solutions
We offer a comprehensive portfolio of electronic test and measurement instruments, ranging
from digital oscilloscopes, microwave and RF instruments, DC and precision instruments, and
modular instruments. Leveraging our product portfolio, we offer flexible solutions that meet the
diverse demands of customers across various industries.
We generally set product prices taking into account technological advantages, raw material
costsandoverallmarketconditions.In2023,2024and2025,weachievedsalesrevenueofRMB670.5
million, RMB775.8 million and RMB900.2 million, respectively. In the same periods, our gross
profit margins were 53.4%, 54.9% and 52.8%, respectively. We have been expanding our product
portfoliobyintroducingmorehigh-performanceproductsandincreasingtheproportionofsolutions
in our sales thereby to increase our profit margin. Throughout the Track Record period, our overall
revenue from product and solution sales consistently grew, with sales rising across all categories.
Our product and solution mix are driven by shifts in customer demand, technological
advancements and the introduction of new products. Based on insights on customer needs and
market trends, we continue to upgrade our existing offerings and launch new products. We see great
potentialtofurthermonetizeourcustomerbase,andweplantocontinuefine-tuningandexpandour
service offerings to expand our customer base. We believe there is a significant opportunity for
profitabilitybyenrichingourportfoliowithpremiumproducts,exploringnewapplicationareas,and
cross-selling more of our solutions. By leveraging our market-oriented innovation capabilities and
marketing activities, our continuously upgraded and expanded product portfolio has propelled our
sustained and robust business growth.
Our Ability to Expand Customer Base and Optimize Sales Channels
We serve a diverse customer base across sectors such as communications, new energy,
semiconductors, and education and research, which has been key to our success. As of December 31,
2025, among the companies on the 2025 Fortune Global 500 list, we had served 100% of the
computer and office equipment companies, 93% of the electronics and electrical equipment
companies, 83% of the semiconductor and other electronic components companies; 100% of the
telecommunication companies; and 77% of the motor vehicles and parts companies. As of the same
date, 87 of the world’s top 100 universities (QS World University Rankings) utilized
RIGOL-branded products. Our future success and revenue growth in particular, is significantly
dependent on our ability to continually attract new customers, expand our sales channels and retain
existing customers.
We sell our products through both direct sales and distributor sales, providing flexibility to
addressdifferentmarketsegments.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,amajorityofourproductswere
sold by distributors. Our collaboration with distributors allowed us to expand in cost-effective
manner, leveraging the resources and local expertise of distributors. To a lesser extent, we also made
directsalesthroughkeyaccountsalesandonlinechannel.Thecompositionofourcustomerbaseand
the effectiveness of our channel management strategies directly impact our revenue growth, market
share, and profitability. We plan to continue exploring opportunities and adjusting our marketing
campaigns to boost brand recognition, ensuring that our expansion efforts lead to increased
profitability and long-term success. To maximize market coverage and sales efficiency, we have
optimized our sales channels. Our ability to adapt our distributor sales channels to market
conditions has been crucial in expanding our business. By building strategic relationships with
distributors, we have extended our market reach and increased sales volume. Through our direct
sales channel, we engage closely with our end customers in particular key account customers,
providing products and solutions that meet their needs. We regularly assess and adjust our sales
channel strategies to respond to market changes and customer demands. This flexible approach
allows us to leverage the strengths of both direct and distributor sales, ensuring comprehensive
market penetration that enhances profitability.

Our Ability to Manage Our Costs and Improve Our Profitability
Our ability to achieve profitability and sustainable growth depends in part on our management
of costs. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our cost of sales was RMB312.3 million, RMB349.9 million and
RMB424.5 million, respectively, accounting for 46.6%, 45.1%, and 47.2% of our revenue for the
same respective periods. Our cost of sales primarily consists of costs of direct materials,
manufacturing overhead, freight, tariff, direct labor and outsourced processing fees. Changes in
any major components of our cost of sales and our overall cost structure could have an impact on
our gross profit. For instance, our direct material costs represent the largest portion of our cost of
sales. The procurement costs for these materials may fluctuate due to a number of factors beyond
our control, such as supply chain disruptions, inflation, and changes in global demand, and we are
susceptible to significant changes in the availability, price and standard of the procured items. We
have implemented cost management measures, including maintaining long-term relationships with
multiple suppliers and establishing the Penang Production Center, to mitigate such risks. Effective
supply chain management, including accurate demand forecasting and inventory control, is essential
to ensuring production continuity and cost efficiency.
Seasonal Fluctuations
Our sales are affected by seasonal fluctuation due to customers’ purchasing practices. The
seasonal ordering trends often result in a higher volume of orders in the second half of the year since
major customers tend to concentrate their order placements toward the end of the fiscal year driven
by their annual budget practices. According to Frost & Sullivan, this is in line with industry norms.
The degree of seasonality may vary each year. Furthermore, our operating and financial results for
an interim period may not be representative of our overall performance for a year.
